put.description:
Author the thesis's catalyst SURFACE — the upcoming binary events the card renders between
entry and exit-by (display objects; the per-name conviction FACTS go through the ratify path).
Full-list replace via the sole writer (``set_catalysts`` — the structural wipe-guard: a promote
never touches this table). Operator authority (#4: the operator authors the events; the platform
times them).

Author the thesis's kill criteria — the documented "what would kill this", read by the
deterministic counter-case (the card stops saying "no documented counter-case"). Full-list
replace via the sole writer; same structural wipe-guard as the catalysts.

Persist the thesis's durable exclusion set (#7) — the operator's NO per name, with the
optional "rejected because X". Full-list replace via the sole writer (the term_set structural
guard, fourth application: a promote never touches the table, so a narrative edit can't wipe
the pruning). THE #9 LINE: discovery never filters on this — a re-draft still surfaces every
name; the EDITOR seeds these as visibly-grayed, one-click-reversible state.

post.description:
APPEND one operator decision (take / pass / close / void) to the decision-capture log.

Advisory only (#5): this LOGS a fill or pass the operator made elsewhere — nothing routes, nothing
blocks. A take against a not-yet verdict is logged with the platform's stance riding the row; that
record IS the v1 gate (the UI shows friction copy — the disagreement is written down, never
enforced). One open position per thesis (v1): take requires flat, close requires open. A mistake
is corrected by ``void`` (an append pointing at the mistaken row — reversibility, never a delete).
The append feeds the Managing state on the next call read (the position derives from this log).

post.description:
Surface an operator-supplied ETF ticker as a ``fund`` sleeve's master row (ETF Sleeve, Slice 1). The
operator TYPES a ticker (e.g. LIT); this resolves it to a ``security_master`` row marked
``instrument_kind='etf'`` — the row the FE then adds to the basket as the sleeve member (the ETF
attaches UNDER a thesis, never free-floating — #2; ``instrument_kind`` is the sleeve's one marker).

LOOKUP-OR-CREATE-AND-MARK, both branches recall-safe: a ticker ALREADY in the master (SPY/GLD — the few
mega-ETFs present as equities) is MARKED ``etf`` in place (``mark_instrument_kind``); a thematic ETF ABSENT
from SEC (LIT/URA/SMH — a fund-trust series, not an operating-company CIK, so ``cik`` resolves to ``None``,
which ``resolve`` already handles) is CREATED via ``resolve(instrument_kind='etf', allow_live=True)`` —
OpenFIGI names it, ``cik=None`` is fine for a price-only sleeve. ``allow_live`` mirrors the extract
endpoint's live-on-an-operator-click precedent (the cost thread: surfacing is an explicit operator click,
never ambient). WRITES the master row (an operational universe write — no thesis spine, no fact, no number,
#3); the operator's promote stays the only spine writer.

NO CALL-PATH TOUCH (#4/#6): the sleeve is an EXPRESSION. ``instrument_kind`` is identity — it never fires,
warms, arms, grades, or vetoes; the events-keyed assembler makes a ``fund`` (which fires nothing) a no-op
for free, so no gate is needed in ``calls/``. NO LLM (#3): a deterministic resolve on a declared ticker.

get.description:
Pull a ``fund`` sleeve's N-PORT holdings and overlap them against the thesis basket (ETF Sleeve,
Slice 2a) — the holdings-seed: *"the ETF holds these N names; here are the M you're missing."*

DETERMINISTIC + EDGAR-NATIVE (#3, no LLM): sleeve ticker → the SEC fund file
(``company_tickers_mf.json``: trust CIK + seriesId, resolved ON-THE-FLY — the trust CIK is never
written to the master, where extraction would misread it) → the series-filtered browse-edgar lookup
(one fetch) → the accession's ``primary_doc.xml`` (immutable-cached) → parsed positions, series
VERIFIED against the requested seriesId. Holdings are quarter-end and ~60 days lagged — fine for a
discovery seed; ``report_date`` labels the vintage and ``source_ref`` links the filing (#6). The
fund INTERNALS (``net_assets`` = AUM + the ``total_assets``/``total_liabs`` composition) ride the
same parsed doc — sleeve-dossier context, never a signal (#4/#6).

THE OVERLAP MATCH is two exact identifier legs, both deterministic (#3): a holding's own N-PORT
``ticker`` identifier when the filer stamped one — else its CUSIP batch-resolved to a US ticker
via OpenFIGI (``figi.map_cusip``, cache-first per CUSIP incl. negative answers, a few rate-limited
POSTs on a first pull). The CUSIP leg is load-bearing: most filers stamp NO ticker on any equity
holding (measured: SMH/URA/LIT all 0 — e.g. SMH's NVIDIA rides only CUSIP 67066G104), so without
it the overlap is empty. Never the master ``cusip`` column (effectively always NULL — a silent
nothing).

RESPONSE-ONLY (#2): no fact, no basket write, nothing persisted — recomputed per click; the
include-a-missing-name flow is Slice 2b, and the operator's promote stays the only spine writer.
NO CALL-PATH TOUCH (#4/#6): holdings are discovery context; nothing here fires, arms, or vetoes.
RECALL-SAFE (#9): the three buckets PARTITION every holding — ``unresolved`` (no ticker AND no
CUSIP, or a CUSIP OpenFIGI can't place on a US line: foreign locals, cash/repo lines) is shown,
never dropped. An explicit operator click (the drawer toggle — the cost thread), live SEC/OpenFIGI
behind the cache seams; requires ``ALPHADECK_USER_AGENT``.

get.description:
Auto-EXTRACT candidate scoring facts for a security from its latest SEC filings (Slice hybrid-1 +
Retrieval Slices 1/A/A-2). A 10-Q/10-K filer gets the three-tier hybrid: AUTO pre-fills the clean
facts, FLAG carries the raw value + a detected risk + the located passage (the operator ratifies the
composition), HUMAN (purity) is LOCATED only and never auto-valued. An issuer with NO 10-K/10-Q (a
foreign private issuer) reads its latest annual filing (20-F/40-F) ONCE and gets — ALWAYS tier FLAG —
honest, current shares from the cover (Slice 1) PLUS cash + span-normalized burn from the financial
statements (Slice A: the RUNWAY meter's inputs, with the located balance-sheet and cash-flow rows as
passages; a cash-GENERATIVE name carries a cash-generative note, never a bogus runway). The statements
are read from the main annual document when they live there, else from the filing's EX-99 statements
EXHIBIT (Slice A-2: the 40-F/MJDS wrapper shape — a bounded, content-signature exhibit hunt; the
passages then cite the exhibit). Purity stays uncovered for annual filers. ``empty_reason`` says WHICH
nothing when there are no facts at all (``no-annual-filing`` vs ``cover-not-located``);
``runway_empty_reason`` is the runway leg's own state when an annual filing exists but no cash_burn
candidate could be read: ``cash-generative`` (a state, not a gap) · ``financials-in-exhibit`` (a
burning name whose statements were in neither the main document nor any exhibit read — deferred,
never a companyfacts-only number) · ``exhibit-ambiguous`` (more than one exhibit reads as the
statements — deferred, never guessed) · ``statements-not-located`` (unread, not empty). An EXPLICIT
operator action (cache-first, live SEC), never fired on a render. The extractor never DECIDES — the
operator confirms (hybrid-2). Requires ``ALPHADECK_USER_AGENT`` (SEC etiquette).

PURITY ESTIMATE (SURFACE 1b): with ``thesis_id``, the grounded purity seam proposes an UNVERIFIED
on-thesis % for the revenue_mix candidate — read ONLY from its located segment passage, with the thesis
narrative selecting the segment. It attaches ``value`` + ``estimate_source="llm_proposed"`` (the passage
stays on the candidate), never a fact until the operator ratifies. PURITY-ONLY: ``thesis_id`` touches no
other candidate, and its absence (or a fail-open decline) leaves purity as today's HUMAN (located, no value).

post.description:
Pull EOD price bars for ONE security — the price leg DECOUPLED from the back-half ingest, so the
finalize screen can complete a name (a real market cap) BEFORE the operator promotes. This endpoint
WRITES (``fact_price_eod``) — deliberately, per explicit click: price bars are FEED data (the same
class as Form 4s), never operator-ratified facts; what they feed (the cap) stays display until the
operator acts.

Bounded + polite by construction: one name per call (the tightest bound — the section button fans out
client-side over a section's members, never the draft); INCREMENTAL (only bars newer than the latest
stored one append — a re-click adds zero rows); CACHE-FIRST (``force_refresh=False``: a first pull on
a fresh name is a cache miss and fetches live; a same-day re-click serves from the cache — the daily
cron, not this endpoint, owns force-refresh). No-lookahead: ``recorded_at`` = now, never backdated.
Shares ONE implementation with ``pipeline.ingest_thesis`` (``ingest_bars_for_security``).

Re-tag one security's BUSINESS TYPE (Business-Type M1) — the operator overruling the maps-derived
classification for ONE name (#10: the maps recommend, the operator decides). ``business_type: null``
CLEARS the re-tag — the visible revert back to derived (reversibility, WB #1). Durable, master-level
identity (what a company DOES holds across theses), stored ONLY when it differs from the derived leaf
(0033 store-on-diff — ``securities/master.set_business_type``). MONITOR display identity, never a fact,
never a call input (#3/#4). The receipt is the security's business-type read AFTER the write.

Draft a plain-English explanation of a FLAG candidate, grounded in its located passage — the one LLM
seam (M4b). A DISPLAY aid shown ALONGSIDE the raw passage; it NEVER becomes a fact.

Note what is absent: no ``get_conn``, no tenant, no write. The explanation rides a separate rail that
dead-ends at the screen — the ratified number can only ever come from the operator's typed field on
``/facts`` (INVARIANT #3). The prompt asks the model not to state the final value; this missing
connection is what guarantees it can't become one.

Fail-open by contract: any LLM trouble (no ``ANTHROPIC_API_KEY``, timeout, SDK error, or the model
declining to ground it) returns 200 with ``{explanation: "", grounded: false}`` — NEVER a 5xx. The facts
panel renders identically to today. (FLAG-only: a non-FLAG candidate returns the same empty signal.)

Promote a structured thesis to the Board (Incubating) — the app's FIRST mutation. Create (``id``
null) or update (``id`` set); the value-chain structure (segments + placements + authorship) persists
via ``thesis_repo.upsert`` (the existing operational save path). The tenant comes from the deployment
resolver, NOT the body. Scores are never sent and never persist — they re-derive on read.

Write-side guards (INVARIANT #2): ``authored_by`` is HONORED from the body for the two live member
values — ``system_drafted`` (the description is the model's draft) or ``operator_edited`` (the operator
edited it — "your words") — so a drafted description stays honestly drafted until the operator actually
changes it. The RETIRED ``operator_set`` (pre-S1 accept/hand-add) is legacy-TRANSLATED, never stored:
``signed_off=true`` + ``authored_by='system_drafted'`` (the 0035 reset rule applied at the wire — old
accept meant ENDORSED, and the text stays the model's). ``signed_off`` itself round-trips as a marker:
it never gates promotion and never feeds the call (#4). Every
placed ``security_id`` must be an EXACT member of this tenant's master (fail-closed — a caller-supplied
id is never trusted), the single point where bound #2 is enforced now that the S5 drafter returns a draft
and writes nothing itself. And the id is CANONICALIZED: a multi-sibling CIK's non-primary row (a foreign
ordinary / warrant / dual-class sibling the draft happened to surface) is re-pointed to the CIK's primary
instrument before the spine write (``master.canonicalize_ids`` — the same pick as ``ids_for_ciks``), so
the basket stores the instrument the operator actually trades; the response carries the canonical
ticker.

THE TWO FIXED LINKS (Context and Bench): every saved thesis carries both as its LAST two links, whatever
the payload sent. The write drops any segment named "Context" or "Bench" in any case (a missing,
mid-list, lowercased or wrongly described one is replaced, never a 422) and appends the two with their
fixed descriptors; a member placed in either one is canonicalized to the exact spelling. A company is
EITHER silent (Context or Bench) OR in the chain, never both: a company holding a Context / Bench row
and any other row (a real link, Discovered, none, or the other silent link) is refused with a 422 naming
it, after the canonicalize and identity passes (sibling listings of one company merge there) and before
anything is written — a row is never dropped silently. A silent name stays on the card but never counts
toward the call (``domain.thesis.voting_thesis``).

THE CONTEXT ROLE (``context_role``, one of six, NULL = unset) is per company per card: it rides EVERY row
of a company, identical. A company whose rows carry two DIFFERENT roles (sibling listings of one company
count as one) is refused with a 422 naming it and the roles it was sent, before anything is written; a
NULL row beside a set role INHERITS that role, so a hand-add or re-draft that puts an existing company in
a second link succeeds; clearing is NULL on every row of the company. Operator-authored display metadata:
it never feeds the call (#4) and no model path writes it (#3).

ON-PROMOTE INGEST (PR-4): a promote that ADDS members (present in the incoming basket, absent from
the pre-upsert spine — diffed by ``security_id``) kicks their back-half ingest as a BACKGROUND job
after the commit, so a fresh starter basket needn't wait for the nightly cron; the additive
``ingest`` field on the response names the job. Deliberately scoped to the genuinely-new members
(the cost thread: every editor Save promotes, so a whole-basket ingest per Save would be ambient
cost); a brand-new thesis is all-new (the full starter-basket ingest); no new members → no job and
``ingest`` null. The job never blocks or fails the promote.

get.description:
X1 — the staged onboarding queue SCOPED to this thesis's members: what the Workbench polls after a
promote whose cold names were queued (``PromoteOut.onboarding``) — counts per status, the pending names,
the latest done ones, the nightly window the job yields to. Read-only. A member with no queue row (its
history was already loaded), or one loaded long ago for ANOTHER thesis, is absent — the counts describe
the names this thesis is still waiting on and the ones its own promotes queued.

POLL an on-promote new-member ingest job (kicked by ``POST /workbench/theses`` when a promote
added members). ``queued`` = waiting behind this thesis's running ingest; ``done`` → the summary of
what landed; ``failed`` → an operator-facing ``error`` (VISIBLE, never silent — the nightly cron
remains the backstop that ingests everything regardless). **404** if the job is unknown / expired,
or the registry was wiped by a restart — the FE shows a visible "lost from view" line (never an
infinite spinner). The job_id must belong to this thesis.

post.description:
Produce + PERSIST the thesis's tiered discovery term set — the SIGNAL/BROAD keywords the EDGAR precision
filter reads. Two sources, two authorities: the operator's ``seeds`` (canonical compounds) are anchored as
``operator_set`` SIGNAL — the RECALL guarantor against keyword-gen's non-determinism — and keyword-gen
PROPOSES the rest, which a DETERMINISTIC guard tiers (``system_drafted``; the "is this discriminating?"
decision is OFF the LLM, ``workbench.term_set``). This is the WRITER seam: the LLM lives HERE, never in
``promote`` (the pure structured writer).

REGENERABLE + CONVERGENT: a re-POST PRESERVES every operator-authored entry — ``operator_set`` seeds AND
``operator_edited`` promotions/demotions (from the edit-UI), each VERBATIM (term + tier + authorship) — while
RE-ROLLING only the ``system_drafted`` LLM-proposed terms. So the inspect-and-tune loop re-rolls the
augmentation without ever dropping an operator decision (a demoted SIGNAL→BROAD term comes back BROAD, not
re-promoted). New ``req.seeds`` are added as fresh SIGNAL. Returns the thesis so the operator can INSPECT the
stored SIGNAL/BROAD split. Fail-open: no key / blank narrative + no seeds → an empty set is stored (the draft
then 503s "term set is empty" — surfaced, never a silent recall fallback). It sources NO number (#3) — terms
only — and writes ONLY ``term_set`` (the narrow ``set_term_set``).

put.description:
SAVE the operator's manually-edited term set DIRECTLY — NO LLM (the LLM lives only in ``POST .../terms``;
this mirrors LLM-out-of-promote, a structural boundary, not a convention). The operator adds a seed
(→ ``operator_set`` SIGNAL), removes a term, promotes BROAD→SIGNAL or demotes SIGNAL→BROAD
(→ ``operator_edited``); an UNTOUCHED ``system_drafted`` BROAD term keeps its authorship so a later
regenerate can re-roll it. Authorship is STAMPED server-side by diffing the stored set
(``stamp_edited_term_set``), never trusted from the body. A full-set replace via the narrow
``set_term_set`` (the SOLE writer; ``upsert`` never names ``term_set`` — the structural wipe-guard stays
intact). Sources NO number (#3) — structure/config only. 422 on an empty term or a case-insensitive
duplicate. An empty ``terms`` clears the set (a visible operator choice; the draft then 503s "term set is
empty").

post.description:
Recommend a tier (signal/broad) + a one-line reason per term in the thesis's term set — the LLM
RECOMMENDS, the operator DECIDES (INVARIANT #10). DISPLAY-ONLY + RESPONSE-ONLY: no writer is called
(``set_term_set`` / ``upsert`` never appear), so a recommendation can NEVER become a persisted tier — it
rides on its OWN wire type (``list[TierRecommendation]``), never on ``ThesisDetail.term_set``, and the
operator confirms it via the EXISTING tier toggle (``PUT .../terms/edit``), where ``stamp_edited_term_set``
stamps ``operator_edited`` (never an LLM-authored SIGNAL). The model judges each term INDEPENDENTLY of its
current tier; the FE does the agree/disagree compare. OFF ``produce_term_set``'s determinism path (advisory
metadata, never a tier the producer applies — recall stays sacred, #9). Fail-open: no key / model trouble ->
``[]`` (the chips render with no recommendation). Sources NO number (#3) — a tier label + a reason string.

schema.title: Response Recommend Tiers Endpoint Workbench Theses  Thesis Id  Recommend Tiers Post

post.description:
KICK OFF the narrative→chain draft as a background JOB and return immediately (**202** + ``job_id``); the
FE polls ``GET .../draft-chain/jobs/{job_id}`` for the result. The draft takes minutes (EDGAR discovery + the
Opus tail-sweep + decompose + narrate); held open as one request it blew past nginx's 300s proxy timeout —
the browser 504'd while the backend kept billing. Only the DELIVERY changed; ``execute_draft`` is unchanged.

The IN-FLIGHT 409 guard lives HERE now (one running draft per thesis — ``DraftInFlight`` → HTTP 409, so a
double-click / stray retry can never launch a parallel Opus pass). The job runs in a daemon thread that opens
its OWN DB connection (it OUTLIVES this request — the ``get_thesis_or_404`` conn is closed once the 202 is
sent). Discovery-not-ready / unexpected faults become a VISIBLE *failed* job on the poll (never a silent empty
draft, #9); a benign fail-open (no key / the model declined) is a *done* job with an empty draft. RESPONSE-ONLY
(the job writes only its in-memory result — no fact, no promote). A completed job additionally dumps a
WRITE-ONLY run-of-record artifact (``data/draft_runs/`` — the DISCOVER stage's ``calls``-log analogue:
the term set as used, the dials, the full draft); nothing in the app reads it, and a failed write is
logged + swallowed, never a failed draft.

The OPTIONAL body carries the draft SCOPE (``DraftChainIn``): absent body (the FE today) or absent field
= ``full`` — byte-identical to the pre-scope draft; ``seeds_only`` is the fast lane (SIGNAL-seeds-only
discovery, no tail-sweep — see ``execute_draft``). The report + the run-of-record name which scope ran.

get.description:
POLL a kicked-off draft job. ``done`` → the ``result`` (a ChainDraftOut); ``failed`` → an operator-facing
``error`` (discovery-not-ready, a timeout, or an unexpected fault — VISIBLE, #9). **404** if the job is
unknown / expired, or the registry was wiped by a restart — the FE shows a visible "draft was lost" (never an
infinite spinner). The job_id must belong to this thesis.

List this thesis's saved draft-run artifacts, newest-first — the run-loader picker's source. Pure file
read (no compute, no EDGAR). **404** when the run loader is disabled (so the FE picker is absent).

schema.title: Response List Saved Runs Workbench Theses  Thesis Id  Runs Get

get.description:
Load one saved run's inner draft as a ``ChainDraftOut`` — the SAME shape the draft endpoint returns, so
the FE hands it straight to the editor's ``applyDraft`` (no re-draft, no refetch). **404** when the loader
is disabled, or for an unknown / traversal ``run_id``; **422** if a stale artifact no longer validates
against the current schema.

Restore this thesis's saved prune session. ``session`` is the stored envelope, or ``null`` for
GENUINELY-ABSENT (no prune saved yet → the FE seeds fresh from the thesis). A read FAULT raises **500**, NOT
a null session — so the FE never mistakes a transient error for "no session" and silently discards a real
prune. Pure file read (no compute, no DB write).

put.description:
Autosave this thesis's prune session — overwrite the single ``latest.json`` with the FE's opaque working
state. Returns the stored envelope (server-stamped ``updated_at``). FAIL-LOUD: a write fault raises **500**
so the operator's "Not saved" indicator is honest (the deliberate contrast with the fail-open draft-run
log). Writes ZERO spine rows regardless of payload — the blob is bytes to a file, never a fact.

delete.description:
Discard this thesis's saved prune session (the operator's explicit "start over" — the ONLY remove; a
promote KEEPS the session so the operator can keep pruning the remainder). Idempotent: deleting an absent
session is a no-op. Returns **204**.

post.description:
Auto-apply a security's AUTO-tier shares count on get-data — REMOVING a ceremonial confirm, not a real one.

The AUTO shares confirm was never a human verification: the operator has no independent knowledge of a
share count and does not look one up, so clicking "Confirm" on a machine-reproduced cover figure rubber-
stamped it while recording ``ratified_by="operator"`` — provenance claiming a check that never happened.
This applies the value directly and stamps it ``ratified_by="auto"``, which is what actually occurred. The
REAL human check is downstream and unchanged: the operator reads the resulting MARKET CAP, a figure they do
have intuition for, and overrides the shares if it looks wrong.

WHY THIS IS NOT A #1/#3 VIOLATION: the written number is the extractor's deterministic reproduction of
filed companyfacts (the market-cap trust class) — never a model output, never a computed/``llm_proposed``
estimate. Estimates remain computed-on-read and MUST NOT become ``fact_*`` rows (see WORKBENCH_EXTRACTION.md);
nothing here touches that. The AUTO tier is exactly the unambiguous single-class, current-cover case —
anything ambiguous trips a FLAG and is excluded below.

THE STRUCTURAL BOUND: the request carries NO value. The server re-extracts (cache-first — get-data just
warmed it) and writes its OWN parse, so no caller can inject a figure under the ``auto`` provenance.

Four gates, each an honest ``applied=False`` rather than an error:
- the security must be in this tenant's master (fail-closed, like ``/facts``);
- ``already_on_file`` — ANY existing shares fact (auto or an operator override) -> no-op. This is the
  idempotency guarantee (a re-run appends ZERO rows) AND the no-clobber guarantee;
- ``not_auto`` — a FLAGged candidate is the operator's to ratify; the machine never resolves a dual-class
  sum or a stale cover;
- ``no_candidate`` / ``no_value`` — nothing to apply.

Ratify an extracted candidate -> write the scoring fact (hybrid-2a) — the app's first fact-WRITE. The
operator confirms/edits a candidate (AUTO as-is, FLAG the composition, HUMAN purity the value); this
persists it via the existing ``ingest_*`` so the meter re-derives on the next scored read.

WRITE-SIDE TENANT DISCIPLINE: the security must be in the CURRENT tenant's master (fail-closed) — the
tenant is the deployment resolver's, but the ``security_id`` is caller-supplied, so a foreign/unknown id

immutable calls log (or a stored edition's frozen pages), the operator-decision log, and realized

``include_annotated`` overrides per request), and rows recorded after their night's next EDGAR
open (by the late-night policy, which ``include_late`` overrides per request). Every reading is
available; nothing is deleted. An edition has none of those rows: its lists come back empty and

What changed from one edition to a later one (editions S6) — computed on read, never stored, and
read-only. Every thesis is compared on the nights BOTH editions cover, through the earlier of the two
editions' last nights (the earlier edition's last night once the later one has reached it), so a night
neither could disagree about is never a change. Edition 0 is read the way the default Scoreboard reads

Per company-night: armed or not in each edition, and — on a night both arm the company — its verdict,
entry grade, conviction grade and exit-by; a night with no page reads that edition's last page before
it. Per episode, paired on (thesis, company, arm date): matched (listed only when the run differs),
moved (the same company armed in both over overlapping windows), appeared, vanished — each scored
arm -> exit-by on realized closes through the last night, with the delta on a pair. Pages only one
edition holds are reported as spans; a run lying wholly on them is counted, never compared, while one
that armed there and runs into the shared nights is a change (``armed_before_window``).

published the later edition from the earlier one (``causes`` true): what its trial proved, or what the
trial's scope implies (late data, a repair or late data, not separated); any other pair has null

get.description:
One episode's realized daily OHLCV bars over ``[start, end]`` — with SMA 50/200 context and four
dated event families — for the Scoreboard drawer's chart (Slice 3, extended in Slice A, widened in
Slice B). The SAME asof-capped read the scorer runs (``PgRealizedPrices``; ``bars_between`` shares
``closes_between``'s cap/known_at), served on demand instead of embedded in the ledger payload (which
stays lean). The line draws ``close``; open/high/low/volume ride the wire for a later candlestick.

Each insider buy carries its server-classified ``character`` (Band 03 S2c — deterministic field
predicates, #3): ``open_market`` / ``self_filing`` / ``primary_market`` / ``implausible``. Set-aside
rows (the last two) ride the wire grayed-and-labeled on the FE instead of being dropped (WB #2 / #9),
so the event ledger shows why a buy did or didn't count toward the panel's open-market flow (#6).

Slice B widens the overlay with three more families through the SAME window + knowability gate:
- ``insider_sells`` — every code-S sale, labeled with the CALL side's screen bucket (wire-mapped:
  ``kept`` / ``planned`` / ``self_filing`` / ``below_low`` / ``implausible`` / ``foreign_ordinary``).
  DIAL-MIRROR CAVEAT: characters are classified with ``DEFAULT_CONFIG`` pinned, so a deployment on
  non-default insider dials could show labels that drift from the call's actual cluster screens —
  the display rail's accepted posture (labels only, never the detector's math).
- ``corporate_events`` — EVERY stored 8-K in-window, ``items`` ``null`` when unresolved (honest,
  never dropped). NO server-side item cut — loudness is a display concern (#9).
- ``activist_stakes`` — the 13D/G tape, both naming eras; unresolved filer identity / ``pct_owned``
  ship as ``null``, the row kept (#9). 13G rows ride — the fire policy stays in the detector.

No-lookahead (invariant #1) is enforced SERVER-SIDE and never trusted to the client, on BOTH axes:
- the price reader caps the valid-time axis at ``cap = asof`` (``d <= asof``), so a client passing a
  future ``end`` still gets only bars ``<= asof`` — the window can never be widened past the as-of. Its
  ``known_at`` stays the reader's default (now), matching the live scorer's construction, so the line
  matches the bars behind the ledger's numbers.
- the insider read caps the transaction axis too (``known_at_for_asof(asof)`` = ``min(now, asof-EOD)``),
  so a scrubbed-back as-of hides not just later bars but later-DISCLOSED buys — the honesty a filing's
  days-to-months disclosure lag demands (the IBM 166-day case), the price bar's ``valid_from == d`` does
  not need.

RELEVANCE FLOOR (Slice A R1): the server bounds the whole window (bars + SMA + insider_buys) to
``[floor, end]`` where ``floor = max(thesis.created_at − 365d, first_bar)`` — a thesis born 2026-07 does
not plot a 2020 buy (off-story, NOT a recall cut). The requested ``start`` is advisory; the response
``start`` is the effective floor so the FE knows the loaded extent (it loads the whole universe and pans
the visible range). The floor is ADDITIVE to the no-lookahead caps above, never a replacement.

SMA is computed over a WARM-UP read (``floor − SMA_WARMUP_DAYS`` through ``end``, asof-capped) so the
left edge is honest, then only bars ``>= floor`` are returned, each annotated (``None`` where too little
history exists — never padded). Prices read under the THESIS'S tenant; a thesis the deployment
tenant can't see is a 404. ``source`` names the fact table the bars came from (invariant #6).
``start``/``end``/``security_id`` ride as bound params — the SQL range fragment stays a trusted literal.

get.description:
The freshness + health summary the admin page opens on — READ-ONLY (writes nothing, owns no
tables). ``record`` measures the calls-log edge against the last EXPECTED Mon-Fri+RUN_AT run
(container-local clock; a Friday edge on a Monday morning is CURRENT — never a weekend false
alarm); ``edge: null`` is the quiet "record has never begun" state. ``last_run`` is the newest
readable run-of-record artifact. ``cron.status`` is the one-word verdict: ``never_ran`` (no
artifact), ``unhealthy`` (the last run froze / errored / totally failed / could not refresh the
shared benchmark tape — as loud as stale, so a bad run can't hide behind green), ``stale`` (the
record missed an expected run), ``gappy`` (the edge is current but a night inside the last
``ALPHADECK_ADMIN_MISSED_WINDOW`` scheduled runs has no call-of-record recorded at/after that night's
``RUN_AT`` — a run that fired on the wrong day, or failed after a daytime pass; the edge check alone
cannot see either), else ``healthy``. ``record.missed_asofs`` lists the holes (empty on a clean
window) and ``record.daytime_only_asofs`` names the subset whose only row is a pre-``RUN_AT`` one.
``tape`` is the FEED freshness panel (G5a price tapes · F1 ETF fund shares): every basket
name whose stored EOD tape or fund-shares sampling has stopped, each row naming which feed, read from
the newest run artifact that evaluated recency — ``null`` until a pass has looked. A stale feed is a
FEED gap, not a cron fault, so it never changes ``cron.status``. A row whose ``closed_at`` is set (G5b)
is a name that CLOSED — delisted / acquired / deregistered per a SEC delisting form filed near its last
bar — so its tape correctly ended and needs no repair; it stays on the panel (never dropped, #9) but
renders quietly as "closed" and never pages. A row with ``renamed`` set (T1) is a repair row whose
company EDGAR lists under other symbols (``edgar_tickers``). ``cron.alarms`` are the status-level
alarms (Phase 1B) that make the verdict
``unhealthy`` though no single run failed: the cron's ``code_sha`` unknown or different from this
backend's (``backend_sha`` / ``cron_sha``), the last live pass paging through the LOG notifier or
running without a User-Agent, and the newest unlabeled DB dump older than the schedule-aware backup
window. ``last_run.audit`` is the latest pass's nightly self-audit; a failed check is a run problem.

M1 — a killed or partial pass never reads healthy. A pass writes its artifact ``running`` at its start
and finalizes it at the end: ``last_run`` is the newest FINISHED pass, and ``unfinished_run`` describes
a newer one that has not finished. Past the sidecar's run timeout (``ALPHADECK_CRON_RUN_TIMEOUT_S``) a
still-``running`` pass alarms "the last pass did not finish", a ``crashed`` one alarms at once, and a
recorded night with no run artifact at all alarms too; inside the timeout the verdict is ``running``.
``record.partial_nights`` judges every window night PER THESIS (the self-audit's own rule): each thesis
in that night's roster needs a non-reconstructed call-of-record at/after ``RUN_AT``, else the night is
partial ("4 of 12 theses") and the verdict ``gappy`` — unless ``pipeline.backfill`` reconstructed that
thesis's night: the backfill resolves the hole, so the night stays QUIET and is listed in
``record.reconstructed_nights`` (a count, never an alarm). The night a pass is still running for is not
judged until it finishes. A LATE row (recorded at/after the next weekday's 06:00 ET EDGAR open) still
covers its night here, but the Scoreboard sets late rows aside (L1), so ``record.late_only_nights`` names
every judged (thesis, night) with a late row and no row the Scoreboard scores — "covered" here, a gap
there.
Informational: it never changes ``reason``, the verdict, or ``cron.alarms``, and never pages.

``split_defects`` (T4) is the split-basis panel — every basket name whose stored tape mixes two split
bases (island / cliff / flap) as some reader sees it, from the newest artifact that scanned; flag only,
never the verdict. Its ``settled`` rows are flaps no reader sees on two bases — quiet, never an alarm.

``missing_closes`` is the missing-closing-price flag: a QUIET line every night ("21 of 679 companies had no
close for Oct 23 at the night's run"), and a LOUD line only for an older session's close still missing after
a later session's pass — from the newest artifact that ran the check; never paged, never the verdict.

The run history — the last N run-of-record artifacts parsed, newest first. A pure FILE read (no
DB, no network, writes nothing); an unreadable/malformed artifact is skipped fail-open so a corrupt
night never blanks the history.

post.description:
KICK OFF the full daily pass as a background JOB and return immediately (**202** + ``job_id``);
poll ``GET /admin/run-daily/jobs/{job_id}``. Fires ONLY on this explicit request — never on a page
load, mount, or poll (cost is the operator's to spend; the pass does a LIVE EDGAR pull and can run
~65 minutes cold). Runs the cron's EXACT unit (``run_daily_pass``): live ingest + call-of-record +
the run-log artifact + the health page — a manual run lands in the run history like the nightly
one. **409** when a run is already in progress ANYWHERE: another process (the cron sidecar, a hand
``pipeline.daily``, a ``pipeline.backfill``) holding the cross-process call-of-record lock, or this
process's own single slot (a double-click can never stack a second pass). The lock is probed here and
then taken for real by the pass itself, which holds it start to finish; a pass that loses the race to
another process in between fails VISIBLY on the poll ("already running"), never runs alongside it.
**503** when the database cannot be reached to check. Safe to re-click once finished: the pass is
idempotent (``record_if_changed`` appends nothing on unchanged facts). The job opens its OWN DB
connection (it outlives this request). **Bounded like the sidecar's pass:** it runs in a child process
for at most the run timeout (``ALPHADECK_CRON_RUN_TIMEOUT_S``, default 5400 s — the one value the
sidecar's ``RUN_TIMEOUT_S`` uses); past it the process is stopped, the run lock is released with it,
its run artifact is marked ``crashed`` and the poll fails with the timeout.

get.description:
POLL a kicked-off daily run. ``done`` → ``result`` (the finished pass, the run-history row
shape); ``failed`` → an operator-facing ``error``. **404** if the job is unknown / expired, or the
registry was wiped by a restart — the run itself may still have completed server-side (the run
history + record edge are the durable authority), so the FE shows "lost from view", never an
infinite spinner.

post.description:
KICK OFF a ``pg_dump`` snapshot as a background JOB and return immediately (**202** + ``job_id``);
poll ``GET /admin/backup/jobs/{job_id}``. Fires ONLY on this explicit request — never on a page load,
mount, or poll (cost is the operator's to spend; the reads may poll, the trigger never does). The dump
is READ-ONLY (``pg_dump``) and mutates no row; it writes a ``.sql`` under ``/data/backups`` (a host
bind, so it is copyable off-box) and prunes old dumps (keep-last-N UNLABELED; a ``label`` marks a
named snapshot, kept 90 days or while among the newest 20 labeled). **409** when a snapshot is
already in progress (the single-slot in-process guard — a double-click can never stack a second
dump). **RESTORE is deliberately CLI-only** (a destructive drop-schema + reload; never a button):
``docker exec -i alphadeck-postgres-1 psql -U alphadeck -d alphadeck < ./data/backups/<file>``. The job opens its OWN subprocess (it outlives this
request).

get.description:
POLL a kicked-off snapshot. ``done`` → ``result`` (the finished ``BackupOut``, the same shape the
list shows — the ``.sql`` on disk is the durable record regardless); ``failed`` → an operator-facing
``error``. **404** if the job is unknown / expired, or the registry was wiped by a restart — the dump
may still have completed server-side (the backups list is the durable authority), so the FE shows
"lost from view", never an infinite spinner.

The snapshot list — every ``.sql`` under the backups dir, NEWEST-FIRST. A pure FILE read (no DB,
no network, writes nothing); an unreadable/foreign entry is skipped fail-open so a stray file never
blanks the list. RESTORE stays a documented CLI act (see ``POST /admin/backup``); this endpoint only
surfaces what exists.

post.description:
ADOPT a renamed name's successor symbol — the operator's ratification of the nightly splice probe.
The symbol must be one EDGAR lists for this name on the newest pass that looked (verified or not: the
probe recommends, the operator decides). Sets ``price_symbol`` through the existing writer (basis
``operator:adopt``) and refreshes the display name from EDGAR's current entity name when it differs;
the change row records the prior values, so ``POST /admin/price-feed/changes/{id}/undo`` restores them
exactly. The next nightly pass re-pulls the tape under the new symbol. **404** unknown security, **409**
not a listed candidate / no rename recommendation / nothing to change, **422** a malformed symbol.

SET a vendor price symbol the operator typed (an unpriceable name — e.g. its TSX listing).
VALIDATED first by ONE live vendor fetch into a throwaway cache: the symbol must return at least one
bar, else **422** and nothing is written. Then set through the existing writer (basis
``operator:set``), recorded with the prior values for an exact Undo. **404** unknown security, **409**
nothing to change, **422** a malformed symbol or no vendor bars.

UNDO an Adopt or a Set — restore the master's prior ``price_symbol`` / ``price_symbol_basis`` (and
``name``, when the Adopt refreshed it) EXACTLY, appending an ``undo`` row (basis ``operator:undo``).
Only the name's standing change, and only while the master still holds its values. **404** unknown
change, **409** already undone / a later change stands / the master moved since.

ACKNOWLEDGE an unpriceable name — "keep it, unpriced" (an append-only ``price_feed_ack``, basis
``operator:acknowledge``). From the next pass the name is QUIET (no page, a quiet count, still listed)
and its vendor 404 counts as expected. Idempotent: an already-acknowledged name returns its active row.
Revoke with ``POST /admin/price-feed/acks/{id}/revoke``. **404** unknown security, **409** the name is
not unpriceable on the newest pass that looked.

REVOKE an acknowledgment — append the inverse row (basis ``operator:revoke``); from the next pass the
name is a loud unpriceable row again (and pages once). **404** when no active acknowledgment has that
id.

MARK a name's price feed with a KNOWN LIMITATION: the vendor serves no history for its symbol, so its
tape builds one bar per night and can never be restated, repaired or backfilled from the vendor (an
append-only ``price_feed_ack`` row ``limited_history``, basis ``operator:limited-history``; the
operator's ``reason`` is REQUIRED). EVIDENCED first by ONE live vendor pull of the name's nightly symbol
(``price_symbol``, else the ticker) at the nightly range into a throwaway cache, stored with the mark:
the vendor must return at least one bar and at most ``LIMITED_HISTORY_MAX_VENDOR_BARS``, else **409** and
nothing is written. QUIET: it pages nothing and quiets nothing on the nightly path — a stopped tape on a
marked name stays a loud stale row and its vendor 404 an error; the named-bar repair's
``no_vendor_bar`` and the name panel note it instead. Idempotent: an already-marked name returns its
active mark (no fetch). Undo with ``POST /admin/price-feed/limitations/{id}/revoke``. **404** unknown
security, **409** no symbol to price / the vendor returned no bars / the vendor serves a history, **422**
a blank reason.

UNDO a feed-limitation mark — append the inverse ``revoke`` row (basis ``operator:revoke``); the
name's notes go away from the next read. The undone mark stays listed (``active: false``), so marking it
again is one click. Returns the mark as it now stands. **404** when no ACTIVE mark has that id (unknown,
already undone, or an acknowledgment — those revoke at ``/acks/{id}/revoke``).

ADOPT a member's SUCCESSOR CIK — the operator's ratification of the nightly successor-CIK detector
(the CIK we store lists no tickers; SEC's ticker map assigns our symbol to this registrant). Only the
CIK the detector RECOMMENDED on the newest pass that scanned is accepted. Re-points
``security_master.cik`` IN PLACE (the row id stays — tape, facts, basket links and sign-off are kept)
and refreshes the CIK-dependent identity from the successor's submissions the detector already read
(``master.enrich`` over ``parse_identity`` — the ``enrich_identity`` derivation — plus the entity name);
the click makes no network request. The change row records every touched column's prior value, so
``POST /admin/price-feed/cik-changes/{id}/undo`` restores them exactly. The next nightly pass reads the
successor's filings. **404** unknown security, **409** no recommendation for this name / not the
recommended CIK / the successor was not read / the master moved since the pass / another master row
already holds that CIK, **422** a malformed CIK.

UNDO a successor-CIK Adopt — restore the master's prior CIK, name and every identity column the Adopt
refreshed EXACTLY, appending an ``undo`` row (basis ``operator:undo``). Only the name's standing
re-point, and only while the master still holds its values. **404** unknown change, **409** already
undone / a later change stands / the master moved since.

get.description:
Every stored Form 4/A with its link, disposition, effective status and evidence, bucketed for the
panel: owed loud (one only you can resolve that touches a buy or sale a live call or an edition page reads —
the ones inside today's signal windows first); applied automatically / decided / unresolved — historical /
queued / inert quiet. Each card says what the filer did, whether any answer changes a call, and what each
button does to the rows a call reads. Read-only.

post.description:
USE THE CORRECTION (basis ``operator:apply``): the amendment as filed replaces its WHOLE original — a void
/ duplicates removes its targets. Allowed over a standing system decision (it stands over it). Undo with
``POST /admin/insider-amendments/decisions/{id}/revoke``. **404** unknown amendment, **409** nothing to
ratify / an operator decision already stands / ambiguous and not linked yet / a correction (it applies).

KEEP THE ORIGINAL (basis ``operator:keep``): the amendment changes nothing — a pending void's
suppression is lifted, and an amendment APPLIED AUTOMATICALLY by the system is overruled (this is that
application's Undo: the keep stands over it, and undoing the keep with the revoke route restores it).
**404** unknown amendment, **409** nothing to decide / an operator decision already stands.

ADD TO THE ORIGINAL (basis ``operator:add``): every original row stands and the amendment's rows are
added beside them — for a 4/A that reports a trade the filer left out. A partial / consolidation / addition /
restatement / field change only. Undo with the revoke route. **404** unknown amendment, **409** a zero-row
or correction amendment (nothing to add) / an operator decision already stands.

LINK an ambiguous amendment to one of its candidate originals (basis ``operator:link``). The
disposition against that original is computed now and stored; a routed one is then pending ratification
(a void suppresses meanwhile). Undo with the revoke route. **404** unknown amendment, **409** not
ambiguous / already linked / not a candidate.

UNDO THE SYSTEM'S PICK (rule 2b — the system linked an ambiguous amendment to the one candidate every
trade it reports matches by shares + price): append ``revoke`` rows (basis ``operator:revoke``) naming the
system's verdict under the pick and its link. The amendment is ambiguous again — its candidates' rows stand,
any candidate can be linked — and it is yours: the nightly sweep never picks it again. **404** no standing
system pick, **409** your own decision stands over the pick (undo it first).

UNDO a standing decision — append a ``revoke`` row naming it (basis ``operator:revoke``); the

get.description:
The run registry, newest first, plus how many runs have touched each dial.

`available: false` when this stack has no backtest store — the normal state on prod.

One run: its manifest, its pooled view, its episodes and its per-thesis ledger.

An unknown run id returns `available: false` rather than a 404, so the page degrades exactly as it
does when the whole store is absent — one code path on the front end, and a stale bookmark reads as
"not here" rather than as an error. A run written before the ledger existed simply has none, and the
drill-down says so rather than rendering an empty table.

Every KEPT curve as a header, newest pass first — what a curve switcher is built from.

A pass writes one curve per dial and `sweep.json` holds only the last of them, so before this the
other five were unreachable from the surface the moment the sixth was written. Headers only: the
points stay behind `/backtest/sweep`, because a listing that parsed every point of every curve would
make the page's cost grow with the store's history.

One sweep curve: the LATEST by default, or a named one from the pass's kept copies.

Unselected, this is `sweep.json` at the store root — latest-only, unchanged, so a link made before
the curves became addressable still resolves to what it always did. Selected, it is the kept copy
under `sweeps/`, and the selection takes THREE parts because one pass may carry the same dial twice —
read pooled and read on one family — and those are two different measurements.

A selection that matches nothing returns `available: false` rather than a 404, the same way an unknown
run does: one code path on the front end, and a stale link reads as "not here" rather than as an
error. Each point cites its own run_id either way, so the runs behind any curve stay addressable
through `/backtest/runs/{id}`.

= identity unresolved; ``pct_owned`` ``None`` = pre-structured era / unparsed. 13G rows ride too —
the fire policy (13D-family originals only) lives in the detector; the FE mirrors it as display
weight (13G-family grayed-passive), never as an omission. ``url`` is the EDGAR filing-index URL
(#6). Both time axes are asof-capped (no-lookahead #1). ``holder`` names a 13D-family original the
call's holder screen sets aside: ``"control holder"`` (a filer row of the filing reports 50% or more
of the class) or ``"insider"`` (a filer is an officer or director of the company on its own Form 4s)
— it stays on the ledger, grayed, and does not fire; ``None`` for every other row.

AdminAcknowledgeIn.title: AdminAcknowledgeIn
AdminAcknowledgeIn.description: Why the operator keeps an unpriceable name unpriced (optional — a default reason is stored).

AdminArrivedCloseOut.description:

of when the feed delivered — never a history gate).

AdminAuditCheckOut.title: AdminAuditCheckOut
AdminAuditCheckOut.description:
One check of a pass's nightly SELF-AUDIT (V1, ``pipeline/self_audit.py``), as the artifact recorded
it. ``ok`` is ``true`` (checked, holds), ``false`` (checked, FAILS — it paged and makes the verdict
``unhealthy``) or ``null`` (NOT APPLICABLE to that pass — e.g. a daytime manual pass cannot leave the
night's on-time row; never read as a pass). ``detail`` is plain English with counts and short ids, never
a thesis name.

AdminCikChangeOut.title: AdminCikChangeOut
AdminCikChangeOut.description:
One operator successor-CIK re-point (``security_cik_change``, migration 0049): an ``adopt`` or the
``undo`` of one. ``prior_cik`` / ``new_cik`` and ``prior_name`` / ``new_name`` are the headline values;
the row also stores every touched identity column's prior + new value — what makes the undo exact.
``basis`` names the author (``operator:adopt-cik`` / ``operator:undo``). ``undoable`` (a standing adopt
only) = the master still holds this change's new values; ``current_cik`` is the master's CIK now.

AdminCronOut.title: AdminCronOut
AdminCronOut.description:
The one-word cron verdict + a plain-English detail. ``unhealthy`` (the LAST run froze / errored /
withheld on total ingest failure / failed to refresh the benchmark tape) is deliberately its own
LOUD state, peer to ``stale`` — a bad run
must read as loud as a missing one, never hide behind green (the R1 freeze lesson). A benign
``--no-live`` dev run is NOT unhealthy. ``never_ran`` = no run artifact at all (quiet). ``gappy`` =
the edge is current and the last run clean, but the recent window has a night with NO call-of-record
(a wrong-day fire) — as loud as ``stale``. Priority: never_ran > unhealthy > stale > gappy > healthy.

``alarms`` (Phase 1B) are the STATUS-level alarms that are not one run's health, each a plain-English
line, and any of them makes the verdict ``unhealthy`` (they are listed even under ``never_ran``): the
cron's last pass ran with an UNKNOWN ``code_sha``; the cron's sha differs from this backend's own (an
image left stale by a partial rebuild) or the backend's own is unknown — compared only for a cron pass
that started after this backend process did, so a full deploy does not read ``unhealthy`` until the
night's pass confirms it; the last live pass paged
through the LOG notifier (``SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL`` unset — a bad night pages nobody) or ran with
``ALPHADECK_USER_AGENT`` unset; the newest unlabeled DB dump is older than
``ALPHADECK_BACKUP_STALE_HOURS`` in schedule time (B4 — only on a stack whose run history shows the cron
sidecar, where a nightly dump is expected). ``[]`` on a clean stack.

M1 adds three alarms and one verdict. Alarms: **the last pass did not finish** (the newest artifact still
reads ``running`` past the run timeout — killed or hung), **the last pass crashed** (``crashed``), and
**rows without a run artifact** (a night has post-``RUN_AT`` rows but no pass artifact at all for it).
``gappy`` now also covers a PARTIAL night (``record.partial_nights``). ``running`` = a pass is in flight
inside its timeout and nothing else is wrong; its own night is not judged until it finishes, so a
healthy pass mid-loop never reads partial or stale. Priority: never_ran > unhealthy > stale > gappy >
running > healthy.

AdminEditionsCutOut.title: AdminEditionsCutOut
AdminEditionsCutOut.description:
The automatic cut (editions S7), as ONE line for seven days after it published the newest Scoreboard
edition — e.g. "Edition 2 · rule change: … · includes data that arrived since Edition 1 · 37
company-nights changed". Backend-authored copy. ``attention`` is true when no declared rule explains the
change (an unexplained change, which also paged).

AdminEditionsNightlyOut.title: AdminEditionsNightlyOut
AdminEditionsNightlyOut.description:
The Scoreboard editions' nightly page job (editions S5), as ONE plain-English line from its newest
APPLIED run artifact (``data/edition_runs``): which edition, which night it paged, how many theses, any held
for history still loading, and the self-check — e.g. "Edition 1 · page for Oct 23 added · 10 theses ·
self-check passed". Backend-authored copy (the FE renders, never composes). ``attention`` is true only when
the self-check found a real mismatch or the job crashed — the one case worth a louder line.

AdminFeedLimitationIn.title: AdminFeedLimitationIn
AdminFeedLimitationIn.description:
Why the operator marks a name's price feed as a known limitation (REQUIRED — the mark is the
operator's statement, so it carries the operator's words; blank is refused).

AdminFeedLimitationOut.title: AdminFeedLimitationOut
AdminFeedLimitationOut.description:
One KNOWN FEED LIMITATION the operator marked (``price_feed_ack`` ``limited_history``, 0056): the
price vendor serves no history for the name's symbol — its tape builds one bar per night and can never
be restated, repaired or backfilled from the vendor. QUIET by design: it pages nothing and quiets
nothing on the nightly path (a stopped tape on a marked name stays a loud stale row); it only lets the
readers that would be loud SOLELY because the vendor lacks history say so.

``active`` = no revoke names it (``revoked_at`` = when it was undone — an undone mark stays listed,
grayed, so marking it again is one click). ``vendor_*`` = the vendor pull that evidenced the mark
(symbol, range, how many bars it returned, the newest); ``tape_stopped`` = the newest pass found the
name's price tape STALE — a real gap the mark does not excuse (``tape_edge`` = its last stored bar).

AdminFilingRefOut.title: AdminFilingRefOut
AdminFilingRefOut.description:
One filing named as evidence (T7): its form, FILING date, accession and — an 8-K-family form — the
item codes EDGAR resolved (``[]`` = none).

AdminFormerNameOut.title: AdminFormerNameOut
AdminFormerNameOut.description:
One of EDGAR's ``formerNames`` for the filer (``since`` / ``until`` as ``YYYY-MM-DD``, ``""`` when
EDGAR omits them) — evidence that the company EDGAR lists under a new symbol is the same filer.

AdminInsiderActionOut.title: AdminInsiderActionOut
AdminInsiderActionOut.description:
One button on the card and what it does to the rows a call reads, relative to the read NOW: ``action`` =
``apply`` (Use the correction) / ``keep`` (Keep the original) / ``add`` (Add to the original) / ``link`` (pick
the candidate ``target``; ``disposition`` = how the 4/A reads against it) / ``undo`` (Undo your decision) /
``undo_pick`` (Undo the system's pick). ``removes`` / ``adds`` = the buy / sell rows the read loses / gains;
``changes_call`` = one of them can be read by a live call or an edition page (the review line).

AdminInsiderAmendmentOut.title: AdminInsiderAmendmentOut
AdminInsiderAmendmentOut.description:
One Form 4/A and everything the operator needs to ratify it.

``disposition`` is what it changed (``domain.insider_amendments``); ``status`` its EFFECTIVE state —
``pending`` (not applied: an ambiguous link, an operator-linked one awaiting a verdict, one the operator
took back, or a pre-R8-B link awaiting the nightly sweep; a pending void/duplicates SUPPRESSES its target
meanwhile), ``applied`` (by the system, or ratified), ``kept`` (the original stands) or ``inert``.
``review`` (R8-B) is where it sits for the operator: ``owed`` / ``auto`` (applied automatically) /
``decided`` (a standing operator verdict) / ``historical`` (ambiguous, but no call reads the rows it
touches) / ``queued`` (the next nightly sweep applies it) / ``inert``. ``suppressing`` = the original
accession(s) it currently removes from every read; ``undo_id`` = the standing OPERATOR decision an Undo
revokes (the verdict first, else the link) — ``None`` on an applied-automatically one, whose Undo is
``keep`` ("keep the original"). ``system_basis`` = the basis of the standing system application
(``system:filer-correction`` / ``system:no-signal-effect``; ``None`` for a correction applied by its link
alone). ``touches_buy`` = a code-P row on either side. ``filing_url`` = the 4/A's EDGAR filing index.

``signal_effect`` = its effect changes a row a call signal reads (a code a registered detector declares,
compared with the owner's role / name and the 10b5-1 flag); ``auto_resolved`` = applied by the system
(``review == "auto"``); ``in_window`` = the signal codes whose changed rows sit inside a signal's live read
horizon today (it can move tonight's call); ``in_review`` = a changed signal row sits inside the review
horizon today (an ambiguous link is owed only then). R8-B's row match (a partial / consolidation / addition
/ restatement / field change): ``kept_rows`` = the original rows (``"<accession>#<seq>"``) the amendment does
NOT account for — they stand, the filer never retracted them; ``unresolved`` = a buy/sell whose date AND
share count both changed (restated, or an added trade? — owed to the operator, the original standing).

The plain-English card (2026-10-24): ``owner_name`` / ``owner_role`` as filed; ``trades`` = the 4/A's own rows
by code, summed; ``usd_total`` = the dollar total of its buys / sells; ``changes_no_call`` = NO answer on this
card can change a row a live call or an edition page reads (the review line — the same test as owed);
``actions`` = each button's effect on those rows; ``pick`` = the system's pick of the original (rule 2b), when
it made or will make one.

AdminInsiderAmendmentsOut.title: AdminInsiderAmendmentsOut
AdminInsiderAmendmentsOut.description:
The "Insider amendments" panel (R8-B). ``owed`` is LOUD — only what the system cannot resolve and a call
can read: an AMBIGUOUS link or an UNRESOLVED row match touching a buy/sell row inside the review horizon
(plus an operator-linked one awaiting its verdict, or one the operator took back), the IN-WINDOW ones first. The rest are QUIET lists,
still visible (#9 / WB#2): ``auto`` (applied automatically — the filer's own correction resolved to its
original, or one that changes no signal row; each with its evidence and its Undo, Keep original),
``decided`` (a standing operator verdict, each undoable), ``historical`` (ambiguous or unresolved, but no
call reads the rows it touches — the originals stand; an ambiguous one still linkable), ``queued`` (a pre-R8-B link the next nightly sweep
applies; a void suppresses meanwhile) and ``inert`` (clerical / no Table I rows / no stored original).
``asof`` is the market day urgency and the review line were judged at. THE REVIEW LINE (what is owed vs
historical): ``review_edges`` = per signal code, the oldest row date a live call or an edition page reads
(``null`` = that code's read is unbounded); ``review_anchor`` = the earliest edition night it was derived from
(``null`` = no edition published: today's windows alone); ``review_horizon_days`` = the pinned dial when it
sets a FLAT window instead (``null`` = derived). Read live from the tables.

AdminInsiderLinkIn.title: AdminInsiderLinkIn
AdminInsiderLinkIn.description: The candidate original the operator links an ambiguous amendment to.

AdminInsiderOriginalOut.title: AdminInsiderOriginalOut
AdminInsiderOriginalOut.description:
A stored Form 4 the amendment touches, with its rows: ``role`` = ``original`` (what it amends),
``voided`` (a duplicate a 1->N void suppresses) or ``candidate`` (an ambiguous link's option). ``filed`` =
its EDGAR filing date (the submissions index, or what the link itself proves; ``None`` = not on file);
``trades`` = its rows by code, summed; ``matched_rows`` = for a candidate, how many of the 4/A's rows it
matches one-to-one by shares + price (rule 2b's count; ``None`` when not judged).

AdminInsiderPickOut.title: AdminInsiderPickOut
AdminInsiderPickOut.description:
Rule 2b — the SYSTEM's pick of an ambiguous amendment's original: the candidate (``target``, with its
``filed`` date), the disposition against it, and the evidence (``matched_rows`` of the 4/A's ``rows`` match
it by shares + price; no other candidate matches them all). ``standing`` = recorded (undo with ``POST
.../undo-pick``); False = the next nightly pass records it.

AdminInsiderReasonIn.title: AdminInsiderReasonIn
AdminInsiderReasonIn.description: Why (optional — a default reason is stored).

AdminInsiderTradeGroupOut.title: AdminInsiderTradeGroupOut
AdminInsiderTradeGroupOut.description:
Every Table I row of ONE transaction code in a filing, summed (the card's "what the filer did"):
``trades`` rows, ``shares`` in all, the price range, the date range, the dollar total (``None`` = no row
states one).

AdminInsiderTxnOut.title: AdminInsiderTxnOut
AdminInsiderTxnOut.description: One Table I row — an amendment's as filed, or a stored original's.

AdminLateOnlyNightOut.title: AdminLateOnlyNightOut
AdminLateOnlyNightOut.description:
One (thesis, night) recorded ONLY LATE (operator decision 2026-10-17): it holds at least one
non-reconstructed call-of-record recorded at/after the night's on-time window closed (the next weekday's
06:00 ET EDGAR open — ``pipeline.night_coverage.is_late``) and NO row the Scoreboard would score (no
non-late, non-reconstructed row — on-time or daytime). The coverage readout counts the late row as
covering the night (the pass did record it), but the Scoreboard sets late rows aside (L1 — they never
define an episode), so there the night is a GAP: listed so "covered" here and the gap there reconcile.
INFORMATIONAL — never an alarm, never the verdict, never paged.

``recorded_at`` = the first late row's stamp and ``edgar_open`` = the window end it missed, both in
market time; ``n_rows`` = late rows on the night. A reconstructed row is never scored, so it does not
fill the gap beside a late row; a reconstructed-only night holds no late row and is never listed (its
own marker, ``reconstructed_nights``).

AdminMasterRefreshOut.title: AdminMasterRefreshOut
AdminMasterRefreshOut.description:
The weekly company-list refresh (``python -m pipeline.populate_master --live --apply``), as ONE
plain-English line from its newest APPLIED run artifact (``data/master_runs``) — e.g. "Company list ·
refreshed Oct 25 · 298 new · 23 renames · 0 conflicts". Backend-authored copy (the FE renders, never
composes). ``attention`` is true only when the run left a CONFLICT (a ticker another company holds — not
applied) or failed: the one case worth a louder line.

AdminMissingCloseOut.title: AdminMissingCloseOut
AdminMissingCloseOut.description:
One company with no stored close for ``session`` (``pipeline/missing_closes.py``) — on the night's quiet
list, or (``loud``) an older session's close still missing after a later session's pass. ``edge`` is its
newest stored bar at that pass; ``reason`` is ``no_bar`` (the price leg ran clean — the vendor had no close
yet), ``fetch_error`` (the leg failed; ``error`` keeps its message) or ``not_ingested`` (another writer held
the company). ``usual_late`` marks a company late at the night's run on most of its recent sessions
(``late_nights`` of ``judged_nights``); ``otc`` a company the master lists on the OTC venue — a KNOWN vendor
issue (``FEED_LOOP.md`` §Known feed limitations). ``ticker`` may be null; the row renders by id (#9).

AdminMissingClosesOut.title: AdminMissingClosesOut
AdminMissingClosesOut.description:
MISSING CLOSES (operator decision 2026-10-23) — did every live basket company get the session's close
by the night's run? Read from the newest finished live run artifact that ran the check (a file read, no
DB). ``line`` is the QUIET nightly line (backend-authored: "21 of 679 companies had no close for Oct 23 at
the night's run (17 OTC, a known issue) · usually arrive with the next night's pull", or "not judged" on a
session with no SPY/IWM close); ``missing`` the companies behind it; ``arrived`` the late closes that
arrived since the previous check (quiet). ``loud_lines`` / ``still_missing`` are the LOUD flag — one line
per older session whose close is still missing after a later session's pass ("2 companies still have no
close for Oct 21: X, Y"); it persists until the bar arrives or the tape goes stale (the stopped-feed list
takes over). Never paged and never the cron verdict. ``error`` = the check could not run on that pass.

AdminNameChangeFilingOut.title: AdminNameChangeFilingOut
AdminNameChangeFilingOut.description: An 8-K carrying item 5.03 (an articles amendment — where a corporate name change is filed).

AdminPartialNightOut.title: AdminPartialNightOut
AdminPartialNightOut.description:
One scheduled night the pass did not fully cover (M1): some thesis in that night's roster has no
call-of-record recorded at/after the night's ``RUN_AT`` and no ``pipeline.backfill`` reconstruction
either (``pipeline/night_coverage.py``). ``covered`` of ``expected`` theses had a live post-``RUN_AT``
row; ``reconstructed_only`` of the rest were backfilled (resolved — they alone never make a night
partial) and ``daytime_only`` have only a pre-``RUN_AT`` row; ``late`` of the ``covered`` ones were
recorded only after the night's on-time window closed (the next weekday's 06:00 ET EDGAR open — a
catch-up the next day). Counts only — never a thesis name.

AdminPriceFeedAckOut.title: AdminPriceFeedAckOut
AdminPriceFeedAckOut.description:
One operator acknowledgment of an unpriceable name (``price_feed_ack``): "keep it, unpriced". Active
= no revoke references it; an active one makes the name QUIET (no page, a quiet count) and its vendor
404 expected (T3). ``still_unpriceable`` = the latest pass still found the name unpriceable (``False``:
it has bars now, so the acknowledgment no longer does anything; ``None``: not in that pass's
inventory).

AdminPriceRepairsOut.title: AdminPriceRepairsOut

AdminPriceSymbolChangeOut.title: AdminPriceSymbolChangeOut
AdminPriceSymbolChangeOut.description:
One operator price-feed repair (``price_symbol_change``, migration 0046): an ``adopt`` (a probed
successor), a ``set`` (a symbol the operator typed, validated by one vendor fetch) or an ``undo``. The
PRIOR and NEW master values ride the row — that is what makes the undo exact. ``basis`` names the
author (``operator:adopt`` / ``operator:set`` / ``operator:undo``). ``undoable`` (a standing change only)
= the master still holds this change's new values, so an Undo would restore the prior state exactly;
``current_symbol`` is the master's price symbol now.

AdminPriceSymbolIn.title: AdminPriceSymbolIn
AdminPriceSymbolIn.description: The operator's chosen vendor symbol (an Adopt of a probed candidate, or a typed Set).

AdminProbeCandidateOut.title: AdminProbeCandidateOut
AdminProbeCandidateOut.description:
One EDGAR-listed symbol for a renamed name, as the nightly splice probe judged it (T2): ``overlap``
= the dates both its vendor tape and our stored tape carry a close on, ``ratio`` = the MEDIAN of its
close / ours over them, ``verified`` = at least 5 shared dates with the ratio within 1% (the same
company's tape under its new symbol). ``bars`` / ``last_bar`` say what the vendor serves under it (whether
adopting it would extend our tape); ``error`` = its one fetch failed (then nothing else is known).

AdminReconstructedNightOut.title: AdminReconstructedNightOut
AdminReconstructedNightOut.description:
A scheduled night some of whose theses are covered only by a ``pipeline.backfill`` reconstruction
(``reconstructed`` of ``expected``), every other thesis having its live post-``RUN_AT`` row. QUIET by
operator decision (2026-10-16): the backfill is the operator's answer to that hole, so the night is NOT
partial and never an alarm — it is listed so the reconstruction stays visible (the Scoreboard reports
such rows and never scores them).

AdminRecordOut.title: AdminRecordOut
AdminRecordOut.description:
The record's freshness vs the LAST EXPECTED scheduled run — never raw ``today - edge``: a
Friday edge on a Monday morning is CURRENT (no run was due yet), the same edge Monday night is 1
behind (stale). ``edge is None`` = the record has never begun — a QUIET state (``days_behind``
None, ``stale`` False), never an alarm on a fresh install.

``stale`` / ``days_behind`` are the EDGE check (MAX(asof) vs the last expected run) and keep exactly
that meaning. ``missed`` / ``missed_asofs`` are the HOLE check: the scheduled weekdays in the last
``window_days`` scheduled runs (ending at ``expected_asof``, never before the record began) with no
call-of-record — a run that fired on the wrong day advances the edge right over the night it skipped,
invisible to the edge check. ``[]`` / ``0`` on a clean window.

**COVERED means a post-``RUN_AT`` row (G2c).** A night counts as recorded only if some call-of-record
for that as-of was ``recorded_at`` at or after that night's ``RUN_AT`` in market time. Mere existence
was too weak: a pre-open "Run daily now" writes a row for today's as-of off the PRIOR session's bars,
so a night whose post-close pass then failed used to read as covered. ``daytime_only_asofs`` names the
as-ofs whose ONLY row is such a daytime one — every one of them also appears in ``missed_asofs``, and
the detail marks them, because "nothing ran" and "something ran, but not after the close" call for
different responses. A next-morning catch-up row is recorded after the cutoff and correctly covers the
night; a ``reconstructed`` row (``pipeline.backfill``) covers it too, unchanged and deliberate.

**PER-THESIS coverage (M1).** ``missed_asofs`` asks whether ANY row landed after the cutoff — so a pass
killed after recording 4 of 12 theses read as a covered night (MEASURED 2026-10-12, healthy for ~18 h).
``partial_nights`` lists every window night NOT in ``missed_asofs`` where some thesis in that night's
roster (created before the cutoff, not archived before it) has no row at/after the cutoff — "4 of 12
theses". A thesis ``pipeline.backfill`` reconstructed is RESOLVED, not missing (operator decision
2026-10-16 — the backfill is the operator's answer to that hole, so a new miss stands out): a night
whose only gaps are reconstructed is not partial and lands in ``reconstructed_nights`` instead, a quiet
count that never changes the verdict. ``[]`` on a clean window; the night a pass is still running for
(within the run timeout) is left out of both until it finishes.

**LATE-ONLY thesis-nights (2026-10-17).** A late row COVERS its night here (the pass recorded it), but
the Scoreboard never scores a late row (L1), so a (thesis, night) with a late row and no row the
Scoreboard would score reads covered here and a gap there. ``late_only_nights`` names every such pair across the same judged
window nights (any thesis with rows for them) — informational, never an alarm: it changes neither
``reason`` nor the cron verdict.

AdminRenamedRowOut.title: AdminRenamedRowOut
AdminRenamedRowOut.description:
A stopped price tape whose company EDGAR lists under another symbol (T1's ``renamed``), with the
nightly splice probe's verdict on each candidate (T2) and the EDGAR evidence — a pending
RECOMMENDATION: nothing is applied until the operator clicks Adopt. ``recommended`` = the first
verified candidate (``null`` = none verified); ``probed`` = the probe judged this row on that pass.
``price_symbol`` is the master's price symbol now; ``change`` the standing operator repair for this name
(an Adopt waiting for the next pass to re-pull, with its Undo), else ``null``.

AdminRunEnvOut.title: AdminRunEnvOut
AdminRunEnvOut.description:
The NON-SECRET environment a pass ran under (I2), as its artifact recorded it: the clock config as
values (``tz`` = the container ``TZ``, ``market_tz``, ``run_at`` = the sidecar's ``RUN_AT``,
``cron_at`` = ``Settings.cron_run_at``) and every secret or delivery switch as a set/unset BOOLEAN only —
no secret value is ever written. ``notifier`` is the class that carried the pass's pages
(``SlackNotifier`` / ``LogNotifier``). Every field is optional so a partial or future artifact parses.

AdminRunJobRef.title: AdminRunJobRef
AdminRunJobRef.description:
The 202 kick-off body — the daily pass started as a background JOB (a cold pass runs ~65 min;
held open it would 504 at the proxy). Poll ``GET /admin/run-daily/jobs/{job_id}`` for the result.

AdminRunJobStatus.title: AdminRunJobStatus
AdminRunJobStatus.description:
The poll body. ``done`` carries the finished pass as ``result`` (the same ``AdminRunOut`` shape
the run history shows — the pass also wrote the durable artifact + calls rows itself); ``failed``
carries an operator-facing ``error``. A 404 on the poll = unknown / expired / restart-wiped job —
the FE shows a visible "lost from view" and points at the run history, never an infinite spinner.

AdminRunOut.title: AdminRunOut
AdminRunOut.description:
One daily pass, as the run-of-record artifact recorded it (``pipeline/cron_run_log.py`` — the
field names are the ARTIFACT's, not inventions): counts + outcomes only, value-free. ``healthy`` /
``problems`` are ``assess_health`` re-read from the same numbers, so the freeze detector
(``edgar_fetches_completed == 0`` on a live run over the theses it processed — O5 — or, on an artifact
that recorded the ratio floor, fewer than that floor of its EDGAR-eligible companies with fresh SEC
data), withheld calls, thesis errors, and a failed BENCHMARK refresh (the shared SPY/IWM tape
``benchmark_rs`` reads — a fail-open passenger leg whose faults used to reach stdout only) surface on
every row — a bad run can never hide behind a green history. The benchmark counts live on the artifact
for exactly that reason; a row written before they existed reads clean, never broken. ``mode`` is
``"live" | "no-live"`` (the R2 recording-gate signal); ``ran_at`` is the artifact's ``started_at`` (UTC
ISO). ``catch_up`` = a ``--catch-up`` pass (the sidecar's boot / late-wake catch-up); an artifact
written before the key existed reads ``False``.

O5 — ``edgar_fetches`` is the EDGAR pulls the pass ATTEMPTED; ``edgar_fetches_completed`` the ones that
returned data, which is what the freeze verdict reads (an empty User-Agent once made 255 attempts and
0 completions, and the attempt count read healthy). ``null`` on an artifact written before O5: that row
keeps the verdict it was paged under (attempts, with a catch-up exempt wholesale).

Phase 1B (each ``null`` / empty on an artifact written before it existed — never an alarm by absence):
``code_sha`` / ``config_hash`` / ``run_kind`` + ``env`` are the pass's RUN IDENTITY and non-secret env
fingerprint (I1/I2); ``audit`` is its nightly SELF-AUDIT (V1) — a failed check is a ``problems`` line
and makes ``healthy`` false; ``name_errors_new`` are the ``"<ticker> (<leg>)"`` labels of names whose
ingest leg started failing that night (O1 — a ``problems`` line with the benign marker: the thesis
still recorded) and ``name_errors_known`` the quiet count of names failing the same way as the pass
before.

``skipped`` (M2) = theses a ``--catch-up`` pass left alone because an ON-TIME call-of-record for the
night already stood (a catch-up never re-records one); ``0`` on every other pass and on an artifact
written before M2.

``split_defects_new`` (T4) are the labels of the split-basis defects that pass flagged as NEW
(``"<ticker> <kind> x<factor> (<date>)"`` — a ``problems`` line with the benign marker: a vendor tape
defect, flag only).

X5 (measurement only, from the artifact's ``timings`` block — ``pipeline/pass_timings.py``):
``pass_total_s`` is the WHOLE pass's wall time, the legs after the per-thesis loop included (unlike
``duration_s``, which ends with the loop); ``top_leg`` / ``top_leg_s`` name the leg it spent the most
time in (``other`` = time no named leg claimed). All ``null`` on an artifact written before X5.

AdminRunsOut.title: AdminRunsOut
AdminRunsOut.description:
The run history — parsed run-of-record artifacts, newest first. An unreadable artifact is
SKIPPED fail-open (a corrupt night never blanks the history).

AdminSplitDefectOut.title: AdminSplitDefectOut
AdminSplitDefectOut.description:
One flagged split-basis defect (T4, ``pipeline/split_basis.py``): a basket name whose STORED price
tape mixes two split bases, as the pass's scan found it. ``kind``:

- ``island`` — a run of bars on another basis than both neighbors (a factor-``k`` step and the inverse
  step back, the volume moving the other way): the half-adjusted shape (VWAV 2026-09-15..16);
- ``cliff`` — a lone UP step whose price stays up and volume stays down by about the same factor: a
  reverse split the vendor never applied to the history before it;
- ``flap`` — a stored bar whose versions changed basis in BOTH directions (the vendor flipped it and
  flipped it back).

``dates`` are the affected bars (at most the 12 most recent; ``events`` is the full count), ``factor``
the step size (>= 1, e.g. 20 for a 1-for-20 split). Evidence for the operator only: nothing here
changes a call (whether a price detector should abstain on a flagged name is an open decision).

AdminSplitJumpBarOut.title: AdminSplitJumpBarOut
AdminSplitJumpBarOut.description: One stored bar after a split-shaped jump (what the price did next).

AdminSplitJumpOut.title: AdminSplitJumpOut
AdminSplitJumpOut.description:
A split-shaped price jump with NO split listed (split plan S5): the close moved x3 or more (or to a third
or less) between two stored bars with the volume moving the other way, the split-night hold has released it
(three sessions on), and no SEC filing or Massive.com row on the list sits near it. A real move or a split no
source has listed yet — the operator's question ("is this real?"). ``step`` = close / prior close.

AdminSplitJumpReasonIn.title: AdminSplitJumpReasonIn
AdminSplitJumpReasonIn.description: Why (optional — a default reason is stored).

AdminSplitListConfirmIn.title: AdminSplitListConfirmIn
AdminSplitListConfirmIn.description: Whose values to confirm: the SEC filing's or Massive.com's.

AdminSplitListEntryOut.title: AdminSplitListEntryOut
AdminSplitListEntryOut.description:
One split on the list (its NEWEST version). ``version_id`` names that version — every action posts it,
and a stale one is refused. ``ratio_from`` -> ``ratio_to`` = old shares -> new shares; ``price_factor`` =
old / new (prices before the split x it). ``decided_by`` is the source label the panel shows ("auto: SEC +
Massive.com", "you, 10-20"). ``actions`` = what the status allows; ``restore_to`` = where Restore returns it.

AdminSplitListOptionOut.title: AdminSplitListOptionOut
AdminSplitListOptionOut.description: One value the operator can confirm a needs-review split with.

AdminSplitListOut.title: AdminSplitListOut
AdminSplitListOut.description:
The "Splits" panel. ``needs_review`` is the one LOUD list (one source could not settle it);
``announced`` (both sources agree, the first session is still ahead), ``confirmed`` and ``set_aside``
(rejected / revoked — kept, grayed) are QUIET lists. ``total`` = every split on the list. Read live.
``unlisted_jumps`` (S5) — split-shaped jumps on basket names that the split-night hold has released and no
