source ever listed, the last 30 days; ``unlisted_jumps_error`` when that read failed (shown, never hidden).
``dismissed_jumps`` — the ones the operator dismissed as a real move (still listed, behind the panel's
"dismissed" filter; each undoable).

AdminSplitListPolygonOut.title: AdminSplitListPolygonOut
AdminSplitListPolygonOut.description: Massive.com's split-reference row: ``split_from`` old shares -> ``split_to`` new shares.

AdminSplitListSecOut.title: AdminSplitListSecOut

AdminSplitOut.title: AdminSplitOut
AdminSplitOut.description:
The split-basis panel (T4), read from the newest run artifact whose scan EVALUATED — like ``tape``,
artifact-sourced so this surface still owns no tables. ``asof`` / ``ran_at`` name that pass;
``window_days`` is the calendar window it scanned (the widest price lookback on the call path).
``defects`` is the full current inventory (one row per name per kind) of the rows some reader sees;
``settled`` the flaps no reader sees on two bases (quiet, never counted as a defect); ``newly_flagged``
the labels that PAGED that night (new since the pass before — a standing defect never re-pages).
``error`` is set when the NEWEST live pass's scan could not run (``defects`` then still shows the last
good inventory, from ``asof``) — a broken monitor is shown, never silently absent.

AdminSplitSettledOut.title: AdminSplitSettledOut
AdminSplitSettledOut.description:
A SETTLED flap (``pipeline/split_basis.settle_flap``): the stored history changed basis and back, but
every night's view reads a single basis — the newest tape has no break, and no night's history view (the
public clock) reads a lookback on two bases. Named so it stays visible, never paged, never an alarm.
``reason`` says how it was judged.

AdminStaleTapeOut.title: AdminStaleTapeOut
AdminStaleTapeOut.description:
One basket name whose monitored FEED has stopped: ``edge`` is the latest stored date for that feed
(``null`` = nothing stored at all), ``thesis`` the thesis it was seen under, and ``kind`` WHICH feed —
``price`` (G5a) or ``fund_shares`` (F1).

Both stop the same silent way — zero rows appended, no error, indistinguishable from a holiday — and
both are dark until repaired: a stopped price tape (the vendor prices the name under a new symbol after
a rename, or it delisted) takes every price-driven detector for that name with it (no breakout, no SMA
flip, no RVOL — and no price-based de-arm), while a stopped fund-shares sample takes an ETF sleeve's
flow read quiet. The REPAIRS differ, which is why the row says which feed it is: the vendor price
symbol on the master for a tape, a fund/ticker/source check for a sleeve. A row from an artifact
written before fund shares were monitored reads ``price``. ``ticker`` may be ``null``; the row still
renders by ``security_id`` and is never dropped (#9).

``closed_at`` (G5b/T1) distinguishes a delisting from a feed gap: when set (a ``price`` row only), it
is the filing date of the SEC delisting form (25 / 25-NSE / 15-12B / 15-12G) filed NEAR the tape's last
bar, on a company EDGAR no longer lists under a different symbol, and the name has legitimately stopped
trading — delisted, acquired, or deregistered — so its tape correctly ENDED and needs no repair. The
panel renders such a row QUIETLY as "closed — stopped trading <date>", distinct from the loud "stale —
repair" rows, and it never pages as newly-stale (#7/WB#3). ``null`` (the common case, and every
``fund_shares`` row) means a feed gap the operator repairs. The name is never dropped from the monitor
(#9) — the marker only reclassifies its stopped tape.

``renamed`` (T1) marks a REPAIR row whose company EDGAR still lists, under symbols that include neither
the master ticker nor its vendor price symbol — a rename the price feed has not followed; the panel
reads "renamed — EDGAR lists <edgar_tickers>". ``edgar_tickers`` is EDGAR's current symbol list as read
by that pass (``[]`` = EDGAR lists none, ``null`` = not read). Both are display only: nothing adopts the
symbol (setting the vendor price symbol stays the operator's repair).

AdminStatusOut.title: AdminStatusOut
AdminStatusOut.description:
The admin page's one-GET summary: record freshness + the newest run + the cron verdict + the
newest DB snapshot + the feed-freshness panel. READ-ONLY — the endpoint owns no tables and writes
nothing (test-proved; the ``last_backup`` join is a pure directory read, and ``tape`` is read from
the run artifacts). ``last_backup`` is ``None`` = the quiet "no snapshots yet" state; ``tape`` is
``None`` until a pass has evaluated feed recency (the quiet "not looked yet" state).

``backend_sha`` is this backend's OWN ``Settings.image_sha`` (``null`` = built without ``GIT_SHA``) and
``cron_sha`` the ``code_sha`` the newest CRON-kind run artifact recorded (``null`` = unknown, or no
cron pass has recorded its identity yet) — the pair the identity alarm compares (I1). The latest
self-audit rides ``last_run.audit``.

M1: ``last_run`` is the newest FINISHED pass (a pre-M1 artifact counts as finished); when the newest
artifact is a pass that has not finished, ``unfinished_run`` describes it (``null`` otherwise).

``split_defects`` (T4) is the split-basis panel — ``null`` until a finished live pass has scanned (a
partial catch-up counts: the scan reads the whole basket union); a defect is a FEED problem (flag
only), so it never changes ``cron.status``.

``price_repairs`` (T2 + Q8 + T3 + T7) is the "Price feed repairs" panel — renamed names with their
splice-verified successors to Adopt, unpriceable names to Set / Acknowledge / Remove, members whose
company now files under a successor CIK to Adopt, the quiet closed and acknowledged names, and every
standing operator repair with its Undo. A feed matter, never the cron verdict.

``splits_needs_review`` (split plan S1) is how many splits on the split list one source could not settle
(one source only, a disagreement, an extractor abstain) — the "Splits" panel (``GET /admin/splits``) holds
them. ``null`` when the count could not be read; never a cron verdict.

``fundamentals_set_aside`` (migration 0062) is how many stored fundamentals versions are set aside — the
revenue rows the data-quality screen would have refused, stored before it existed, which every read skips
(``python -m pipeline.set_aside_fundamentals``). A quiet line; ``null`` when the count could not be read.

``editions_nightly`` (editions S5) is the Scoreboard editions' nightly page job's one line, from its newest
applied run artifact; ``null`` until that job has run (a directory read — no DB). Never a cron verdict.

``missing_closes`` (2026-10-23) is the missing-closing-price flag: the night's quiet count line and, loud,
any older session's close still missing after a later session's pass; ``null`` until a live pass has run
the check (a file read — no DB). Never paged, never a cron verdict.
``editions_cut`` (editions S7) is the automatic cut's one line for seven days after it published the
newest edition (a DB read of that edition); ``null`` otherwise. Never a cron verdict.
``master_refresh`` is the weekly company-list refresh's one line, from its newest applied run artifact
(``data/master_runs``; a directory read — no DB); ``null`` until it has run. Never a cron verdict.

AdminSuccessorCandidateOut.title: AdminSuccessorCandidateOut
AdminSuccessorCandidateOut.description:
One CIK SEC's ticker map now assigns the member's symbol to (T7), with the evidence read from ITS
submissions on that pass: ``matched_on`` = our symbols the map assigns to it; ``entity_name`` /
``former_names`` / ``edgar_tickers`` = who EDGAR says it is; ``succession_filings`` = its 8-K12B /
8-K12G3 (the successor-issuer report). ``recent_foreign_form`` / ``files_domestic_forms`` /
``incorporation`` preview the identity an Adopt applies (``identity_read`` false = the successor's
submissions could not be read that night — then ``error`` says why and the row is not adoptable).

AdminSuccessorCikIn.title: AdminSuccessorCikIn
AdminSuccessorCikIn.description:
The successor CIK the operator adopts (T7) — digits, with or without the zero padding; it must be
the CIK the nightly detector recommended for the name.

AdminSuccessorRowOut.title: AdminSuccessorRowOut
AdminSuccessorRowOut.description:
A basket member whose company now files under a NEW CIK (T7's detector): the CIK the master holds
lists no tickers on EDGAR, and SEC's ticker map assigns the member's symbol to another registrant — a
pending RECOMMENDATION; nothing is applied until the operator clicks Adopt. ``stored_cik`` and the OLD
CIK's evidence (``old_entity_name``, ``old_former_names``, its ``deregistrations`` — 15-12B / 15-12G /
15-15D) sit beside each ``candidates`` entry's. ``recommended`` = the one candidate (``null`` when the
map is ambiguous — shown, not adoptable). ``current_cik`` is the master's CIK now; ``change`` the
standing operator re-point for this name (an Adopt waiting for the next pass, with its Undo).

AdminTapeOut.title: AdminTapeOut
AdminTapeOut.description:
The FEED freshness panel (G5a price tapes · F1 ETF fund shares), read from the newest run artifact
that actually EVALUATED recency — not a fresh DB scan, so this surface still owns no tables. ``asof`` /
``ran_at`` say which pass produced it (the answer is "as of last night", which is the right
granularity for a nightly feed).

``stale_days`` and ``fund_shares_stale_days`` are the thresholds **that pass judged under**, read off
its artifact rather than live, so the number shown always describes the list shown even if the setting
changed in between; each feed has its own because their cadences differ (a price tape gets a bar every
session, while a sleeve's sample carries the source page's own stated as-of date). ``0`` means that
feed's monitor was disabled for the pass.

``stale`` is the full current inventory, one row per feed per security (a name placed in several
value-chain links appears once; a name stale on both feeds appears once per feed, since the repairs
differ — each row's ``kind`` says which). A row with ``closed_at`` set is a name that CLOSED (delisted /
acquired / deregistered), G5b — it stays in this inventory (never dropped, #9) but renders quietly and
is absent from ``newly_stale``. ``newly_stale`` are the display labels that PAGED that night — the diff
against the previous evaluated pass, so a known-dead feed does not re-page forever, and a closed tape
(an expected event, not a feed gap) is never in it (#7/WB#3).

AdminThesisRefOut.title: AdminThesisRefOut
AdminThesisRefOut.description: A thesis holding a name (``id`` + ``name``) — where the operator goes to remove it from the basket.

AdminUnfinishedRunOut.title: AdminUnfinishedRunOut
AdminUnfinishedRunOut.description:
The NEWEST run artifact, when its pass has not finished (M1): the pass writes its artifact with
``status: "running"`` at its start and finalizes it at the end, so a ``running`` newest artifact is a
pass in flight — or, once older than the sidecar's run timeout (``timeout_s``, the C2 ``RUN_TIMEOUT_S``),
a pass that was KILLED (the VM went down, the timeout fired) and will never finish (``past_timeout``).
``crashed`` = an exception escaped the pass (``error`` names it). Either of the dead shapes is a
``cron.alarms`` line; a pass still inside its timeout reads ``running``, never an alarm.

AdminUnpriceableRowOut.title: AdminUnpriceableRowOut
AdminUnpriceableRowOut.description:
An UNPRICEABLE basket name (Q8): no stored price bar ever, and neither closed (T1) nor renamed (T2)
— WONDF's shape. Loud until the operator ratifies one of: set a price symbol (validated by one vendor
fetch), acknowledge it ("keep it, unpriced"), or remove it from the basket in the editor (``theses``).
``vendor_error`` is what the price leg got that night (a 404); ``edgar_tickers`` what EDGAR lists
(``[]`` = none). ``change`` = a standing operator Set (waiting for the next pass, with its Undo).

AnnotatedNightOut.title: AnnotatedNightOut
AnnotatedNightOut.description:
One phantom-arm night (D3b): a (thesis, as-of) whose recorded row carries an ACTIVE ``exclude``
annotation — under the default reading it is set aside like a reconstructed night; under the
``include_annotated`` reading it is scored. ``reasons`` are the annotation tokens (e.g.
``stale_comparative_revenue``), ``rules`` the code identities that judged it
(``d3a-first-knowability@<sha>``), ``n_rows`` the annotated rows on the night.

Authorship.title: Authorship
Authorship.description:
Who placed a basket member in its value-chain segment (the Workbench authorship seam).

The MVP writes only the operator values; ``SYSTEM_DRAFTED`` is present now so the seam already
supports the bounded LLM drafter (the next slice) without a later schema change.

AutoConfirmOut.title: AutoConfirmOut
AutoConfirmOut.description:
The outcome of an auto-confirm — honest about WHY nothing was written.

``applied=False`` is a normal, expected result (a FLAGged name, a name already on file), never an error:
the caller fires this optimistically after get-data and the server decides. ``reason`` names which gate
stopped it so the UI (and a test) can tell "we declined to auto-apply" from "it failed".

AutoConfirmRequest.title: AutoConfirmRequest
AutoConfirmRequest.description:
Ask the server to auto-apply a security's AUTO-tier shares count (the get-data path).

NOTE WHAT IS **NOT** HERE: a value. The client cannot supply the number — it names a security and a
fact type, and the SERVER re-extracts and writes its OWN deterministic parse. That is the structural
bound (INVARIANT #3): an auto-applied fact can only ever be the extractor's reproduction of filed
companyfacts, so no client bug or caller can inject a figure under the ``auto`` provenance.

``fact_type`` is deliberately a ONE-value Literal: only the AUTO shares count is eligible. Purity is the
operator's edge (HUMAN, never auto-valued) and cash_burn stays a manual ratify — extending this is a
decision, not a parameter.

BacktestLedgerOut.title: BacktestLedgerOut
BacktestLedgerOut.description:
The run's episode ledger — the PER-THESIS drill-down, in the Scoreboard's own wire vocabulary.

It reuses `ScoreboardReplayThesisOut` / `ScoreboardEpisodeOut` deliberately: the rows ARE replayed,
scored arm episodes, and re-declaring a parallel shape would give the two surfaces two definitions
of the same row and let their renderers drift. The front end therefore renders this through the
same ledger components the Scoreboard's own ledger uses.

A DRILL-DOWN, never a ranking: theses come back in NAME order (fixed by the writer), which is the
one ordering that cannot be read as a leaderboard (invariant #4). The pooled view above it carries
no thesis identifier at all; this is where a reader checks a pooled number against its own rows.

Its metrics are the run's own, over the ELIGIBLE set only (matured + non-censored — the Scoreboard's
rule), which is a smaller set than the pooled panel scores. The two are never pooled into one
number, and the banner says so.

BacktestManifest.title: BacktestManifest
BacktestManifest.description:
Everything needed to reproduce, or to refuse to trust, one run.

Nothing here is optional-by-accident. ``hypothesis`` and ``decision_rule`` are nullable only because a
bare exploratory run at the default config is a legitimate thing to do; the CLI REQUIRES both the moment
an overlay is supplied, so no run that moved a dial can exist without its pre-registration.

BacktestRunResponse.title: BacktestRunResponse
BacktestRunResponse.description:
One run: what it IS (the manifest), what it FOUND pooled, and its episodes for the drill-down.

The manifest and the pooled report are served as THEMSELVES — the artifact's own models, published
straight onto the wire. They were designed to be read (that is what a manifest is for), the route is
read-only, and re-declaring ~60 fields here would only create a second place for the artifact's
shape to drift from itself.

`episodes` stays an untyped pass-through, deliberately and for the opposite reason: the front end
reads exactly the BREADTH fields off it (co-arm counts, the Key-1 source, the confirmation grade),
those fields ride THIS response rather than widening the Scoreboard's `ScoredEpisode`, and a run
written by an older or newer engine must degrade to missing fields rather than fail validation on a
read-only research surface.

BacktestRunSummaryOut.title: BacktestRunSummaryOut
BacktestRunSummaryOut.description: One registry row — enough to pick a run without opening it.

BacktestSweepRefOut.title: BacktestSweepRefOut
BacktestSweepRefOut.description:
ONE CURVE'S HEADER — what a reader picks by, never its points.

A store accumulates curves and a switcher that listed them would otherwise parse every point of every
one. These are the fields a choice is made on (which pass, which dial, which slice, which window,
what was pre-registered) plus the two that decide whether two curves may be read together AT ALL: the
clock they were swept on and the mirror they were swept over.

BacktestSweepResponse.title: BacktestSweepResponse
BacktestSweepResponse.description:
One sweep curve.

`sweep.json` at the store root is LATEST-ONLY and is what comes back when nothing is selected — a
bookmark from before the curves were addressable still resolves. With a selection it is the KEPT copy
under `sweeps/`, which is what makes a pass's other curves reachable: a six-dial pass wrote six, and
five of them were unreachable the instant the sixth landed.

The curve itself rides as an opaque object on purpose. It is the sweep report's own model, published
by the writer and read by the surface; re-declaring ~20 fields here would create a second place for
the artifact's shape to drift from itself, and the surface already degrades field by field (a curve
written before a field simply does not carry it).

BacktestSweepsResponse.title: BacktestSweepsResponse
BacktestSweepsResponse.description: Every kept curve, newest pass first. `available: false` when this stack has no store.

BackupCreateIn.title: BackupCreateIn

BackupJobRef.title: BackupJobRef
BackupJobRef.description:
The 202 kick-off body — the snapshot started as a background JOB (``pg_dump`` runs ~30-90s). Poll
``GET /admin/backup/jobs/{job_id}`` for the result.

BackupJobStatus.title: BackupJobStatus
BackupJobStatus.description:
The poll body. ``done`` carries the finished snapshot as ``result`` (the same ``BackupOut`` the
list shows — the ``.sql`` on disk is the durable record regardless); ``failed`` carries an
operator-facing ``error``. A 404 on the poll = unknown / expired / restart-wiped job — the FE shows a
visible "lost from view", never an infinite spinner.

BackupOut.title: BackupOut
BackupOut.description:
One snapshot as a value-free file listing — ``name`` (``alphadeck-<UTC>[-<label>].sql``),
``bytes`` (file size), ``created_at`` (parsed from the filename timestamp, UTC), and ``labeled``
(a named dump: kept 90 days, or while among the newest 20 labeled, rather than in the rolling
keep-N). Computed on read from the backups directory; writes nothing.

BackupsOut.title: BackupsOut
BackupsOut.description:
The snapshot list — newest first. A pure directory read; an unreadable/foreign entry is skipped
fail-open (the run-log read discipline).

BusinessSupersector.title: BusinessSupersector
BusinessSupersector.description:
The business-type SUPER-SECTOR — the coarse watch grouping above the leaf ("are the utilities
moving?"). Pure code map from the leaf (``securities/business_type/supersectors.csv``), zero
storage, re-drawable without a migration. Identity like ``BusinessType``; never a call input.

BusinessType.title: BusinessType
BusinessType.description:
WHAT a company DOES — the business-type LEAF (MONITOR/organization identity, Business-Type M1).

Derived on read from the master's stored ``sector`` (EDGAR ``sicDescription``) via the editable
data files in ``securities/business_type/`` — descriptive IDENTITY like ``sector``/``origin``
(#1/#3 govern numbers, not identity strings): never a fact, never a call input, never fires/arms/
vetoes/grades. ``OTHER`` is the visible tail (an unmapped-but-present sector — never a silent
drop, #9); an un-enriched row derives ``None`` (unclassified — the honest abstain). This enum is
the TYPE CONTRACT; the SIC→leaf DATA lives in ``sic_map.csv`` (operator-editable).

BusinessTypeOut.title: BusinessTypeOut
BusinessTypeOut.description:
The re-tag receipt: the security's business-type read AFTER the write, re-derived server-side —
what every scored surface will now show (#6: the response shows the effective state, not an echo).

CallCardResponse.title: CallCardResponse
CallCardResponse.description: The CallCard as served — the domain card plus resolved provenance URLs.

CatalystIn.title: CatalystIn
CatalystIn.description:
One catalyst-surface entry (a narrative binary event the card's surface renders between entry
and exit-by) — display objects, distinct from the conviction FACTS (``RatifyCatalyst``). Server
generates the id; the list is replaced whole (the operator edits it as a list).

CatalystType.title: CatalystType
CatalystType.description: The catalyst nature, where one applies (optional on a signal; extensible).

ChainDraftOut.title: ChainDraftOut
ChainDraftOut.description:
The narrative→chain draft (Slice 5b): the value-chain SEGMENTS the model proposed + each proposed name
resolved against the master to PLACED / AMBIGUOUS / ABSENT (exact membership decides — INVARIANT #2).

RESPONSE-ONLY and value-free: it carries NO score/number field, and the endpoint persists NOTHING — a
placed name is UNSCORED until the operator extract→ratifies it, and the operator's promote is the only
writer. ``segments`` / ``placements`` reuse the resolver's domain result types directly (the wire is the
resolver's output). ``report`` is the run's honesty report (coverage / capped terms / tail-sweep /
narration — ``DraftReportOut``): ALWAYS set by ``execute_draft``, optional on the wire only so a reader
handles its absence.

ContextRole.title: ContextRole
ContextRole.description:
What part a company plays on THIS card — the operator-authored CONTEXT ROLE on a basket membership
(Context roles, Phase 1). Display metadata only: stored, carried end to end, shown quietly, and never read
by the call (#4 — the operator decides what a company is to the thesis, never the model, #3). A later
phase reads signals from a role-tagged company's own disclosures (a "read-through"); that is not built.

NAMING GUARD: this is NOT ``BasketMember.role`` (the free-text prose field) and NOT ``SignalEvent.role``
(``Role``: entry_trigger / risk_signal). ``None`` on a member = unset, never a default. The labels and
hover descriptions the operator reads live in the frontend; the wire/DB values are these.

CorporateEventOut.title: CorporateEventOut
CorporateEventOut.description:
One stored 8-K filing inside an episode's window (Slice B) — an overlay chip / ledger row.

``d`` = ``valid_from`` = ``filed`` (an 8-K is knowable exactly when EDGAR disseminates it, so the
one event clock plus ``ingested`` suffices — no separate ``disclosed``). ``items`` is the SEC's
own item-code list; ``None`` = not-yet-resolved, rendered honestly as "items unresolved", never
dropped (#9). ``url`` is the EDGAR filing-index URL (#6). EVERY stored 8-K in the window rides —
there is NO server-side item cut (loudness is a display concern; a cut would be a silent filter).
Both time axes are asof-capped (no-lookahead #1).

CrossCardOut.title: CrossCardOut
CrossCardOut.description:
A card a name sits on in this group: its ticker there (the Cockpit's ``?name=`` key) and its links
there (``null`` = Unsegmented).

CrossClusterOut.title: CrossClusterOut
CrossClusterOut.description:
A group where ``count`` of its ``priced`` names crossed ``direction`` within ``recent_sessions`` (at
least ``cluster_min_names`` and ``cluster_min_share_pct``% of them), all within ``within`` sessions, with
``rs_leaders`` of them at a 13-week relative-strength high.

CrossFirstMoverOut.title: CrossFirstMoverOut
CrossFirstMoverOut.description:
A group where exactly one priced name crossed ``direction`` within ``recent_sessions``. The group's
``rest`` priced names: ``closing_in`` (near-crossing the same way), ``already`` (on the far side with no
recent cross: above the 200d for golden, below for death) and ``not_yet``.

CrossGroupOut.title: CrossGroupOut
CrossGroupOut.description:
One group. Link view: ``link`` (``null`` = Unsegmented) + its card. Card view: the card. Business type
/ Sector view: ``business_type`` / ``supersector`` (``null`` = Unclassified). ``names`` = the companies in
the group, each counted once; ``priced`` of them have a 200-day SMA at the as-of.

CrossMarkOut.title: CrossMarkOut
CrossMarkOut.description: One cross on the timeline: ``pos`` is its column on ``sessions`` (0 = the oldest).

CrossNameOut.title: CrossNameOut
CrossNameOut.description: A name's recent cross: its date and how many sessions before the as-of it printed.

CrossNearNameOut.title: CrossNearNameOut

CrossPostureOut.title: CrossPostureOut
CrossPostureOut.description:
The group's names by ``sma_position`` posture; ``other`` = every other posture and every name not
priced.

CrossRadarOut.title: CrossRadarOut
CrossRadarOut.description:
The whole page in one view, each list in its default order (clusters by share then count; first
movers newest cross first; near-cross by the smallest gap; the timeline by total crosses). The counts are
the work shown on its quiet line; the rule dials ride along. ``sessions`` = the timeline's axis.
``cache`` / ``compute_ms`` = whether the heavy read was served from the shared dashboard cache and how
long it took when it ran.

CrossTimelineNameOut.title: CrossTimelineNameOut
CrossTimelineNameOut.description:
One company of a timeline row. ``crosses`` = every 50d × 200d cross of the last ``history_sessions``
sessions, newest first (``readable_sessions`` of them could be read: a name with a shorter tape reads a
shorter history); ``price_200d`` = its price × 200d crosses when that layer is on. A name ``not_priced``
(``short_tape`` / ``stale_tape``) reads no crosses.

CrossTimelineRowOut.title: CrossTimelineRowOut
CrossTimelineRowOut.description:
One group's crosses over the last ``history_sessions`` sessions (``golden`` / ``death`` count every
cross), the price × 200d counts when that layer is on, and its posture bar.

DataFlagEvidenceOut.title: DataFlagEvidenceOut
DataFlagEvidenceOut.description: One piece of evidence behind a flag: a label, and a link when the source has one (an SEC filing).

DataFlagOut.title: DataFlagOut
DataFlagOut.description:
One data issue on one name, as of the view's day (``domain/data_flags.py``). ``level``: ``in_doubt``
(the number is shown grayed, the reason on hover) or ``known_wrong`` (the number is not shown: "—" with
the reason). ``columns`` = the Cockpit cells it reaches (empty = no number on the row is touched: shown in
the panel and Admin only). ``dates`` = the bars the Scoreboard chart shades. ``call_affected`` = the
split-night hold is holding this name's price triggers on the call card.

DataFlagSplitOut.title: DataFlagSplitOut
DataFlagSplitOut.description:
One split on the list as the NamePanel and the chart label it: announced (``sec_filed``), confirmed
(``confirmed_by``), took effect (``took_effect``), history corrected (``corrected_on`` — only when Alpha
Deck re-scaled the vendor's bars before it). ``factor`` = prices before ``effective_date`` x factor.
``bars_ago`` = how many bars the first bar at the new price sits before the view's newest bar.

DataFlagsResponse.title: DataFlagsResponse
DataFlagsResponse.description:
The data flags as of ``asof`` (computed on read, never stored). ``thesis_id`` is set on the per-thesis
read (members with a flag, a marker or a split row) and null on the union read (members with a flag or a
marker). ``names`` = how many names were judged.

DataNoteOut.title: DataNoteOut
DataNoteOut.description:
A quiet marker on one name: information, not a defect (``short_price_history``). It never marks the row
or grays a cell. ``since`` = when the condition began, ``until`` = when it stops applying.

DecisionIn.title: DecisionIn
DecisionIn.description:
One operator decision to APPEND (gate-1 ratified 2026-07-10). Advisory only (#5): this LOGS a
fill/pass the operator made elsewhere — nothing routes, nothing blocks. ``take`` opens the thesis's
(single, v1) position; ``close`` closes it; ``pass`` records a no-act (any state, reason optional);
``void`` points ``voids`` at a mistaken row — the reversibility inverse, never a delete.

DecisionOut.title: DecisionOut
DecisionOut.description:
One logged decision. ``call_state``/``call_verdict`` are the platform's stance when it was
logged (display denormalization — attribution re-derives from the calls-log join); ``voided``
marks a row a later ``void`` points at (the strip grays it — visible, never hidden).

DisplayBasis.title: DisplayBasis
DisplayBasis.description:
Show-the-work for a computed indicator (#6): the fact table it read, the parameters, and the
exact bar window used — plus a staleness note when the tape lags the asof.

DisplayEvent.title: DisplayEvent
DisplayEvent.description: A dated flip/cross the tape actually printed — display context, never a trigger.

DisplayHeadline.title: DisplayHeadline
DisplayHeadline.description:
A member's one-glance state chip, rendered at the top of its block.

``key`` is a STABLE machine state (a future Board column / basket cell can consume the
categorical directly); ``label`` is the literal statement, always derived from the member's
params (never a hardcoded window or MA type — change fast/slow/SMA→EMA and the words follow);
``glyph`` is a token the FE maps to a subtly-tinted arrow; ``detail`` is the muted secondary
read. A headline states the tape, it never forecasts (#4).

DisplayMetric.title: DisplayMetric
DisplayMetric.description:
One labeled reading. ``value=None`` is an HONEST gap — the ``note`` says why ("n/a: 140/200
bars"), never a fake number (#6 show the work, #7 quiet degrade).

``tone`` opts a DIRECTIONAL metric into a green/red (pos/neg) render — set ONLY where the sign is
a genuine up/down read (ETF net flow: inflow vs outflow, where a bare minus is too quiet), left
None everywhere else so a non-directional chip stays neutral. The FE renders it generically off
this field, so a future directional member colors with zero frontend change.

DisplaySeries.title: DisplaySeries
DisplaySeries.description:
A compact, FIXED-SLOT ordered series a member emits for a SHAPE read (the basket table's
sparkline) — e.g. the last N closes. ``values`` is ascending by bar and index-spaced (one slot
per trading bar, the tape's own convention — never calendar-spaced), newest LAST. A ``None``
slot is an HONEST gap — no bar there: a thin tape is LEFT-padded to the window so a young name
draws a shorter, right-aligned path, never a line stretched to look like a full window — and the
FE breaks the line on it, never interpolates (#6/#9). The exact tape behind the slots rides the
signal's ``basis`` (``bars_used``, ``window_start``/``window_end``). Display context only: a
series has no role and no scalar, so it cannot fire, sort, rank, or grade (#4).

DisplaySignal.title: DisplaySignal
DisplaySignal.description:
A display member's output: f(point_in_time_data, security_id, asof) -> DisplaySignal | None.

Structurally NOT a ``SignalEvent``: no role/fired/grade/score, so it physically cannot turn a
key, veto a window, or ride the recorded CallCard. ``kind`` is the registered member name.

DisplaySignalsResponse.title: DisplaySignalsResponse
DisplaySignalsResponse.description:
Read-only per-name display indicators, re-derived from the bitemporal facts at ``asof``.

Display-only tape context beside the call — NEVER a SignalEvent, never an input to the call,
and never recorded: a day-varying field on the recorded domain CallCard would break the daily
cron's ``record_if_changed`` idempotency (one appended calls row per night), so indicators ride
this compute-on-read endpoint instead. See ``docs/DISPLAY_SIGNALS.md``.

DraftChainIn.title: DraftChainIn
DraftChainIn.description:
The OPTIONAL draft kick-off body — the draft SCOPE. ``full`` (the default; an ABSENT body or field
means full, so today's no-body FE kick-off is untouched) runs the whole pipeline; ``seeds_only`` is the
fast lane: discovery enumerates ONLY the term set's SIGNAL seeds — the operator's own ratified anchors —
and the Opus tail-sweep is skipped outright (never invoked). Scope narrows the INPUT the operator chose,
never the results (#9 stays whole: nothing found is dropped, and the report names which scope ran).

DraftCoverageOut.title: DraftCoverageOut
DraftCoverageOut.description:
How much of the universe the draft's EFTS enumeration actually covered (the #9 rule-2/3 instrument on
the wire): a sub-threshold gap used to pass looking complete (logged only); now the pages fetched vs
attempted — and the TERMS whose pages are still missing — ride every draft to the operator. RUN state,
display-only, never persisted.

DraftJobRef.title: DraftJobRef
DraftJobRef.description:
The 202 kick-off body — the draft started as a background JOB (it takes minutes; held open it 504'd at the
proxy). The FE polls ``GET .../draft-chain/jobs/{job_id}`` for the result. Only the DELIVERY changed; the
draft logic is unchanged.

DraftJobStatus.title: DraftJobStatus
DraftJobStatus.description:
The poll body. ``done`` carries the ``result`` (the ChainDraftOut); ``failed`` carries an operator-facing
``error`` (discovery-not-ready, a timeout, or an unexpected fault — VISIBLE, never a silent empty draft, #9).
A benign fail-open (no key / the model declined) is ``done`` with an EMPTY draft, not a failure.

DraftReportOut.title: DraftReportOut
DraftReportOut.description:
The draft run's honesty report — every formerly-silent recall-loss mode, named per run (#9 rules 2/3):
EFTS coverage, the hit-capped terms (enumeration truncated at the cap — deep hits not searched), the
tail-sweep outcome (``ran`` / ``failed`` / ``skipped`` — a failed sweep is no longer indistinguishable from
"no foreign names exist"), and the narration fill (M of N placed/verify names carrying thesis-fit prose).
Value-free (#3) and RESPONSE-ONLY — display run state, never a fact, never persisted; the Workbench strip
renders it quiet at 100% healthy, loud on any gap (inverse loudness).

EditTermsRequest.title: EditTermsRequest
EditTermsRequest.description:
Body for ``PUT /theses/{id}/terms/edit`` — the operator's full, edited term set, saved DIRECTLY (no LLM,
mirroring LLM-out-of-promote). Authorship is re-stamped server-side: an untouched ``system_drafted`` BROAD
term keeps its authorship so a later regenerate can re-roll it; only operator-touched entries become
``operator_set`` (added) / ``operator_edited`` (re-tiered). An empty list clears the set (a visible operator
choice).

EditionCompanyDiffOut.title: EditionCompanyDiffOut
EditionCompanyDiffOut.description:
One company that changed: every changed night (``nights``), the same nights folded into runs
(``runs``), and its episode changes.

EditionCompanyNightOut.title: EditionCompanyNightOut
EditionCompanyNightOut.description:
One changed company-night: ``changed`` = ``["armed"]`` when exactly one edition arms the company, else
the fields that differ on a night both arm it. ``cause`` (S7) is set only when the later edition was cut
by the automatic cut from the earlier one: ``rule_change`` / ``unexplained`` (its rules trial proved it,
with or without a declared rule), ``late_data`` (a night the rules trial re-tested and found unchanged),
``data_repair`` (a repair trial: a repair or data that arrived late, not separable), ``not_separated``
(a night the rules trial did not re-test, or a trial that also carried a deleting repair). Null for any
other pair of editions — a cause is never guessed.

EditionCutNoticeOut.title: EditionCutNoticeOut
EditionCutNoticeOut.description:
The quiet notice for seven days after the AUTOMATIC CUT (editions S7) published the newest edition:
``line`` is the backend-authored sentence ("Edition 2 · rule change: … · includes data that arrived since
Edition 1 · 37 company-nights changed"), ``number`` / ``previous`` the pair the "see what changed" link
compares, ``unexplained`` true when no declared rule explains the change (the edition is marked).

EditionDiffCountsOut.title: EditionDiffCountsOut
EditionDiffCountsOut.description: The headline counts over every thesis (company-nights and episodes).

EditionEpisodeDiffOut.title: EditionEpisodeDiffOut
EditionEpisodeDiffOut.description:
One episode change, paired on (thesis, company, arm date): ``matched`` (same arm date, listed only when
the run differs — ``differs`` names what), ``moved`` (the same company armed in both over overlapping
windows, ``arm_shift_days`` apart), ``appeared`` (later edition only), ``vanished`` (earlier edition only).
``return_delta`` = later minus earlier score when both are scored. ``armed_before_window`` (appeared /
vanished) = the run armed before the first compared night and is listed because it runs into the nights
both editions cover. ``cause``: as on a company-night (null unless the later edition was cut from the
earlier one).

EditionEpisodeSideOut.title: EditionEpisodeSideOut
EditionEpisodeSideOut.description:
One edition's arm episode, scored through the comparison's last night (``forward_return`` = arm ->
exit-by on realized closes). ``began_mid_arm`` = armed on that edition's first page for the thesis.

EditionJoinOut.title: EditionJoinOut
EditionJoinOut.description:
The episode's company's join date in an edition (``edition_entry``): the date, whether it is the
option-A ESTIMATE (a deploy-seed member whose real join predates the snapshot record), the rule that
produced it, whether the arm fell on that estimated night, and the drawer's backend-authored note.

EditionNightReadOut.title: EditionNightReadOut
EditionNightReadOut.description:
One company's read on one night in one edition: ``page`` = the page it comes from (the night itself,
or that edition's last page before it — the Scoreboard's own carry rule), ``armed``, and — only on an
armed night — the call's verdict, entry grade, conviction grade and exit-by.

EditionNightRunOut.title: EditionNightRunOut
EditionNightRunOut.description:
Consecutive compared nights on which one company's change is the same (the same ``changed`` fields
with the same values of those fields on both sides, and the same ``cause``) — ``nights`` folded so a
30-night run reads as one line; ``before`` / ``after`` are the reads on its first night.

EditionNightSpanOut.title: EditionNightSpanOut
EditionNightSpanOut.description: A run of one edition's pages the other does not cover (``n_nights`` pages, ``first`` -> ``last``).

EditionThesisDiffOut.title: EditionThesisDiffOut
EditionThesisDiffOut.description:
One thesis: the nights compared (``first_night`` -> ``last_night``, the ones BOTH editions cover; null
when they share none), the pages only one edition holds (``before_only`` / ``after_only`` spans, with
``n_outside`` unpaired runs lying wholly there — counted, never compared), the nights its own state differs,
the matched-episode count, the armed companies with nothing to list, and the companies that changed.

EpisodeOperatorOut.title: EpisodeOperatorOut
EpisodeOperatorOut.description:
The operator's answer to an arm episode: took (with the operator's own prices/return —
``inferred`` marks a close used where no fill price was logged) or passed (no prices; the
episode's own outcome sits beside it). No delta fields — v2.

EtfHoldingOut.title: EtfHoldingOut
EtfHoldingOut.description:
One holding on the wire (ETF Sleeve, Slice 2a). ``ticker`` is the holding's best-known ticker —
the filing's own where it carried one, else (for a held/available match) its CUSIP resolved to a US
ticker via OpenFIGI; ``None`` only when nothing matched (``unresolved``). ``cusip``/``isin`` are the
FILING's own identifiers, carried alongside as provenance (coverage varies by filing agent — some
stamp no ticker at all). Plus the weight and — for the held/available buckets — the matched master
``security_id``.

EtfHoldingsOut.title: EtfHoldingsOut
EtfHoldingsOut.description:
A ``fund`` sleeve's N-PORT holdings + basket overlap (ETF Sleeve, Slice 2a) — RESPONSE-ONLY
discovery context, recomputed per click, never persisted (the operator's promote stays the only
spine writer, #2).

``report_date`` is the holdings VINTAGE (N-PORT is quarter-end, ~60 days lagged — fine for a
discovery seed); ``source_ref`` the EDGAR filing index URL the whole answer traces to (#6). The
three buckets partition ALL ``holdings_count`` positions — ``held`` (in this thesis's basket) ·
``available`` (in the master, not the basket) · ``unresolved`` (no master match — SHOWN, never
dropped, #9). Weight-sorted, heaviest first.

The fund INTERNALS ride the SAME N-PORT (no extra fetch): ``net_assets`` = AUM (the fund's size),
with the ``total_assets``/``total_liabs`` composition it nets down from (net = gross − liabilities).
Display-only context on the sleeve dossier — never a signal (#4/#6); ``None`` if a filer omits them.

Evidence.title: Evidence
Evidence.description: Immutable reference to a filing / data point.

ExcludedName.title: ExcludedName
ExcludedName.description:
One durably-excluded name (#7): the operator's NO, with the optional why. Applied by the
EDITOR as pre-seeded grayed state — discovery never filters on it (#9, recall sacred).

ExclusionIn.title: ExclusionIn
ExclusionIn.description:
One durably-excluded name (#7): the operator's NO with the optional why. Full-list replaced
via the sole writer; discovery never filters on it (#9) — the editor grays, visibly.

ExtractedFact.title: ExtractedFact
ExtractedFact.description:
One candidate scoring fact for a security, with its tier, raw value(s), located evidence, and flags.
The shape mirrors the three ``ingest_*`` writers: shares -> ``value``; cash_burn -> ``cash_usd`` +
``quarterly_burn_usd``; revenue_mix (purity) -> no value (HUMAN).

ExtractionResult.title: ExtractionResult
ExtractionResult.description:
The extract endpoint's envelope (Retrieval Slice 1): the candidates plus an HONEST reason when
there are none. The three empty states are DISTINCT (interaction #2 — "we couldn't read it" must
never masquerade as "there is nothing"; the old bare ``[]`` + the FE's *"nothing to extract or
ratify here"* copy was false for 44 of the 48 dark names):

- ``facts`` non-empty → covered. For an annual-cover name that is SHARES ONLY — cash + purity are
  still not covered for it (the FE says so rather than implying the data doesn't exist).
- ``empty_reason="no-annual-filing"`` → no 10-K/10-Q AND no 20-F/40-F: genuinely nothing on EDGAR
  the extractor can read (SKHY, a brand-new F-1/DRS listing). The only case where "nothing to
  extract" is true.
- ``empty_reason="cover-not-located"`` → an annual filing EXISTS but its cover instruction could
  not be matched: the name is UNREAD, not empty — it stays a visible candidate for the next
  pass, and companyfacts alone is deliberately NOT served (a fact without its located passage
  would break the no-passage-no-fact contract).

``runway_empty_reason`` (Retrieval Slice A) is the RUNWAY leg's own honest state for an annual
filer whose filing exists but yielded no cash_burn candidate — kept SEPARATE from ``empty_reason``
because the shares leg usually still emits (facts non-empty), and the three states must stay
distinct (interaction #2):

- ``"cash-generative"`` → operating cash flow is positive: a STATE, not a gap — no runway applies
  and none is computed (a finite number here would be bogus).
- ``"financials-in-exhibit"`` → a BURNING name whose financial statements were found in NEITHER
  the main document NOR any EX-99 exhibit the bounded scan read (Retrieval Slice A-2 hunts the
  exhibits by content signature — both statement rows — before this reason fires): deferred,
  never a companyfacts-only number (no passage → no fact).
- ``"exhibit-ambiguous"`` → MORE THAN ONE exhibit carries the statement signature (Slice A-2's
  fail-closed rule): deferred rather than guessed — a wrong statement source is the runway
  analog of a confident-wrong cover match.
- ``"statements-not-located"`` → neither the statements nor a companyfacts sign could be read:
  unread, not empty.

pct_armed_with_a_co_member.title: Pct Armed With A Co Member

FiringDiagnostics.title: FiringDiagnostics
FiringDiagnostics.description: Counts and mixes — NO outcome, so no hindsight risk. This is what catches a broken detector.

FlagExplanationOut.title: FlagExplanationOut
FlagExplanationOut.description:
The model-drafted, plain-English explanation of a FLAG candidate, shown ALONGSIDE the raw passage.

Deliberately carries NO value field: it is display-only and never rides the ratify rail (the ratified
number comes solely from the operator's typed field on ``RatifyFactRequest``). ``grounded=False`` (with an
empty ``explanation``) is the honest no-explanation / fail-open signal — the UI shows the raw passage and
manual ratify exactly as today. (INVARIANT #3.)

HealthResponse.title: HealthResponse
HealthResponse.description:
The ``/health`` body. ``status`` is ``"ok"`` or ``"degraded"``; ``degraded`` maps each degraded
subsystem to a short reason (empty when healthy). The compose healthcheck only needs the HTTP 200 —
``degraded`` is a body flag an operator or agent can SEE, never a failed check (fail-open).

IdeaTimelineDecisionOut.title: IdeaTimelineDecisionOut
IdeaTimelineDecisionOut.description:
A take / close / pass at its ``decision_date``; ``voided`` = a later void row names it (shown grayed,
never hidden).

IdeaTimelineHatchOut.title: IdeaTimelineHatchOut
IdeaTimelineHatchOut.description:
A stretch of a segment whose nights' winning rows are ``reconstructed`` (reported, never scored) or
carry an active ``exclude`` annotation (``excluded``: set aside on the Scoreboard, ``reason`` its
reason). ``end`` is exclusive.

IdeaTimelineOut.title: IdeaTimelineOut
IdeaTimelineOut.description:
The whole page. The axis runs from the earliest recorded night to today, then on to the latest future
marker, capped at ``future_cap`` (today + 90 days). The counts are the work shown on its quiet line.

IdeaTimelineRowOut.title: IdeaTimelineRowOut
IdeaTimelineRowOut.description: One live card. ``current_state`` is ``null`` for a card with no recorded call yet (no segments).

IdeaTimelineSegmentOut.title: IdeaTimelineSegmentOut
IdeaTimelineSegmentOut.description:
One run of the same recorded state. ``verdict`` = its first night's; ``end`` is exclusive (the next
run's first night, or today for the current run); ``days`` = ``end - start`` in calendar days.

IngestJobResultOut.title: IngestJobResultOut
IngestJobResultOut.description:
A done ingest job's summary — what landed, per fact kind (append counts from the run's
``NameResult``s; re-versioned rows are folded in, matching the CLI's tallies). Counts only, never a
signal or a score.

IngestJobStatusOut.title: IngestJobStatusOut
IngestJobStatusOut.description:
The ingest-job poll body. ``queued`` = waiting behind this thesis's running ingest (one follow-up
run, never a parallel one); ``done`` carries the ``result`` summary; ``failed`` carries an
operator-facing ``error`` (the per-name partial-failure summary, a timeout, or an unexpected fault —
VISIBLE, never silent; the nightly cron remains the backstop either way).

InsiderBuyOut.title: InsiderBuyOut
InsiderBuyOut.description:
One code-P insider purchase inside an episode's window (Slice A, characters in Band 03 S2c) — an
overlay chip / event-ledger row.

``d`` = the transaction date (``valid_from``, the chip's x-position). TWO honest clocks (the MRVL
two-clock fix — invariant #6): ``disclosed`` = the real SEC acceptance date (``accepted::date``, when the
filing became public), ``None`` when unresolved (pre-backfill / unresolvable — the FE renders the
"ingested" line only, recall-safe #9); ``ingested`` = ``recorded_at::date`` (when OUR pipeline wrote the
row), rendered as a SECOND line only when it differs from ``disclosed``. On the rebuilt demo a Form 4
accepted ~2d after its txn but re-ingested in 2026 reads "disclosed 2d later · ingested 326d later" —
honest, where the old single ``disclosed=recorded_at`` field lied "disclosed 326d". ``aff_10b5_1``
(TRUE/FALSE/NULL) flags a Rule 10b5-1 pre-scheduled plan (a note rendered only on an explicit TRUE,
never a different number). Every field traces to a real ``fact_insider_txn`` row; both time axes are
asof-capped (no-lookahead, #1). A LIVE read gates on ``recorded_at``; a past-asof view reads the PUBLIC
clock (operator decision 2026-10-21), where ``accepted`` IS the row's gate — so a buy shows only once it
was public, and ``ingested`` stays bookkeeping.

``character`` is the buy's server-side classification (deterministic field predicates — #3, the same
predicates the NamePanel's open-market screen composes): ``open_market`` means "passed the available
screens", NEVER "proven discretionary" — a buy with no day-low price context stays ``open_market``;
``self_filing`` = the issuer filing a Form 4 on its own stock (labeled, still counted in the panel's
90d net-flow — that re-base is deferred); ``primary_market`` (an offer-price IPO/PIPE/placement
subscription) and ``implausible`` (bad source data) are SET-ASIDE rows the panel's open-market figure
excludes — surfaced grayed + labeled instead of hidden (WB #2), so the ledger shows why a buy did or
didn't count (#6). The chart's non-set-aside dots reconcile with the panel's net-flow.
``internal_transfer`` = a buy matched to a sale between LINKED filers (``domain.insider_internal_transfers``
— James Kim's AMKR shares moved to his children's partnership): set aside like the call sets it aside;
``transfer_with`` names the counterparties.

``private_passage`` / ``private_counterparty`` — a buy the filer's OWN footnote says was a private purchase
(``domain.insider_private_purchases``: a deterministic phrase list, the passage located verbatim — never a
model). Display only: the buy still counts (a private purchase between unrelated people is real
conviction); the FE renders the quiet note ("private purchase from Joshua Harley — not on the open
market"). The counterparty is named only when grounded (a same-day seller on this tape the passage names,
or the issuer). Both ``None`` when no passage is located.

InsiderSellOut.title: InsiderSellOut
InsiderSellOut.description:
One code-S insider sale inside an episode's window (Slice B — the sell mirror of
``InsiderBuyOut``): an overlay chip / event-ledger row.

Same shape and the same two honest clocks as the buy (``d`` = transaction date; ``disclosed`` =
``accepted::date``, ``None`` when unresolved → the FE falls back to the "ingested" line, #9;
``ingested`` = ``recorded_at::date``), both time axes asof-capped (no-lookahead #1, the
``recorded_at`` gate like every fact table).

``character`` is the sale's server-side classification via the CALL side's sell screen
(``signals.insider_sell._screen`` — deterministic field predicates, #3), wire-mapped
(``self`` → ``self_filing``, ``foreign`` → ``foreign_ordinary``): ``kept`` = what the risk
detector's cluster counts; ``planned`` (an explicit 10b5-1 True — near-noise), ``self_filing``
(the issuer transacting its own stock), ``below_low`` (a discounted secondary — a different risk
family), ``implausible`` (bad source data), and ``foreign_ordinary`` (a home-market ordinary line
mis-filed on the ADR's tape) are SCREENED rows — surfaced grayed + labeled instead of hidden
(WB #2), so the ledger shows why a sale did or didn't count (#6).

DIAL-MIRROR CAVEAT: the labels are classified with ``DEFAULT_CONFIG`` pinned — a deployment
running non-default insider dials could show characters that drift from the call's actual cluster
screens. The display rail's accepted posture; labels only, never the detector's math.

``internal_transfer`` = a sale matched to a buy between LINKED filers (``domain.insider_internal_transfers``
— a transfer within the filer group, never insider supply), screened like the call screens it;
``transfer_with`` names the counterparties (``None`` on every other sale).

InstrumentKind.title: InstrumentKind
InstrumentKind.description:
What an instrument IS on the security master — the modular foundation brick (ETF Sleeve, Slice 1).

``EQUITY`` = a common-stock operating company (the default; every existing master row). ``ETF`` = a fund
the operator SURFACES as the low-torque ``fund`` sleeve expression of a thesis. Operator-DECLARED, never
auto-detected. Descriptive IDENTITY (like ``sector`` / ``category``): it never feeds a number on a call
card and never gates the call path — the sleeve is an EXPRESSION, never a call input (#4/#6). Future
callable kinds (``spac``, …) extend this enum WITHOUT another migration+backfill.

KeyState.title: KeyState
KeyState.description: One of the two keys (Conviction / Confirmation) rendered on the call card.

KillCriterionIn.title: KillCriterionIn
KillCriterionIn.description:
One kill criterion — the operator's documented "what would kill this thesis"; feeds the
deterministic counter-case (the card stops reading "no documented counter-case").

reason.title: Reason
reason.default: recorded after the next EDGAR open

LateNightOut.title: LateNightOut
LateNightOut.description:
One late night (L1, operator Q5 = A): a (thesis, as-of) holding a call-of-record recorded at/after
its night's on-time window closed — the next weekday's 06:00 ET EDGAR open — so it can have read a
filing SEC accepted after the night. Under the default reading such rows are set aside before the
per-as-of dedup; under the ``include_late`` reading they are scored. ``recorded_at`` = the first late
row's stamp, ``edgar_open`` = the window end it missed, ``n_rows`` = late rows on the night,
``earlier_recorded_at`` = the stamp of the earlier honest row the late-excluding reading scores instead
(``null`` = none: the night reads like a cron gap), ``reason`` = the words.

LeadersCardOut.title: LeadersCardOut
LeadersCardOut.description:
A card a name sits on: its ticker there (the Cockpit's ``?name=`` key) and its links there (``null`` =
Unsegmented).

LeadersClusterNameOut.title: LeadersClusterNameOut
LeadersClusterNameOut.description: A name of an insider-cluster group: its open-market buys and distinct buyers in the last 30 days.

LeadersInsiderGroupOut.title: LeadersInsiderGroupOut
LeadersInsiderGroupOut.description:
A group where at least ``group_min_names`` names had open-market buys in the last 30 days. Link view:
``link`` (``null`` = Unsegmented) + its card. Card view: the card. Business type / Sector view:
``business_type`` / ``supersector`` (``null`` = Unclassified). ``with_buys`` of its ``names`` (each counted
once) bought, ``share`` = ``with_buys / names``; ``no_insider_data`` of them have no Form 4 ingested;
``buys`` = the group's buys.

LeadersListOut.title: LeadersListOut
LeadersListOut.description:
One list: its names (``security_ids`` into ``names``, in its default order) and how many companies in
view its display ``member`` gave no reading (not on the list for want of data, never silently dropped).

LeadersNameOut.title: LeadersNameOut
LeadersNameOut.description:
One company on at least one list (``lists``), each list's value beside it. ``pct_off_high`` = % off the
52-week closing high (``high_date`` its print date; ``range_bars`` the bars the range stands on, under
``full_year_bars`` = not a full year); ``rs_vs`` = the benchmarks its RS is at a 13-week high against;
``contraction`` = the vcp member's newest-segment depth over its oldest; ``buys_30d`` / ``buyers_30d`` =
open-market buys and distinct buyers in the last 30 days (``cluster`` = at least ``cluster_min_buyers``
buyers); ``rvol20`` = RVOL 20D. ``null`` = no reading.

LeadersOut.title: LeadersOut
LeadersOut.description:
The whole page in one view. ``names`` = every company on at least one list, in the several-lists order
(the number of lists, then the 30D return); ``several`` = those on ``multi_min_lists`` or more; ``lists`` =
each list's names in its default order and its no-reading count; ``insider_groups`` by names with buys,
then share. The counts are the work shown on its quiet line; the rule dials ride along. ``cache`` /
``compute_ms`` = whether the heavy read was served from the shared dashboard cache and how long it took
when it ran.

LocatedPassage.title: LocatedPassage
LocatedPassage.description:
A deterministically-retrieved passage that backs a fact — the evidence put in front of the operator
(or, later, S5). Retrieval only: a keyword/section match, never a model's reading.

MemberCallOut.title: MemberCallOut
MemberCallOut.description:
One basket member's call in the per-member ranked menu (M5 Part A). `armed_members` is ranked
(the headline is [0]); `watch_members` are confirmation-only ("moving, no conviction yet").

MemberDataFlagsOut.title: MemberDataFlagsOut
MemberDataFlagsOut.description:
One name's flags, quiet markers and split rows. ``marked`` = some flag reaches a cell on its row (the
row mark); a marker never sets it.

MemberDisplaySignalsOut.title: MemberDisplaySignalsOut
MemberDisplaySignalsOut.description:
One resolved basket member's read-only indicators. ``signals: []`` = nothing computable at
this asof (e.g. no ingested bars yet) — an honest empty, the member still shows.

MetricWithNulls.title: MetricWithNulls
MetricWithNulls.description:
A pooled metric and the two things it must be read against.

``actual`` alone is uninterpretable on a universe assembled with hindsight. ``vs_timing`` and
``vs_name`` are the same statistic over the two null distributions, and ``excess`` strips the theme's
own drift by measuring against the basket's equal-weight move over the identical window. A reader who
quotes ``actual`` without them is quoting the operator's stock-picking, not the algorithm's timing.

MirrorInfo.title: MirrorInfo
MirrorInfo.description:
The frozen Parquet mirror this run swept, and what it does NOT contain.

``excluded_tables`` + ``blind_detectors`` are a pair on purpose: naming a table that was left out is
only half an answer, because the reader still has to work out what stopped firing. Saying both means a
result can never be read as "that detector is inert on this tape" when the truth is "that detector had
no tape".

OnboardingNameOut.title: OnboardingNameOut

OnboardingReadoutOut.title: OnboardingReadoutOut
OnboardingReadoutOut.description:
X1 — the staged onboarding queue as the operator reads it (``pipeline/onboarding.readout``): ``counts``
per status (+ ``parked``), the PENDING names (failed first), the latest done ones, the latest run, the
nightly window the job yields to, and ``stalled`` (names waiting with no finished run for
``Settings.onboard_stalled_after_h`` — LOUD). Quiet unless a name failed or the queue stalled (WB#3).

OnboardingRunOut.title: OnboardingRunOut
OnboardingRunOut.description:
X1 — the latest run of the onboarding job (its artifact, ``data/onboard_runs``): ``stopped`` = why it
ended (``done`` / ``window`` / ``pass_running`` / ``budget_names`` / ``budget_time`` / ``daily_cap``),
``counts`` = names per outcome (``done`` / ``requeued`` / ``failed`` / ``yielded`` / ``busy`` / ...).

OperatorSpanOut.title: OperatorSpanOut
OperatorSpanOut.description:
An off-record take→close span (answering no armed episode), with the stance FROZEN on the
take row at logging time. ``override`` = entered while the platform said not-armed — the
gate's logged override, now carrying its outcome.

PooledReport.title: PooledReport
PooledReport.description:
The whole pooled view. Deliberately carries NO thesis identifier of any kind — see the module
docstring; a test walks this payload to keep it that way.

Position.title: Position
Position.description: Populated once the operator logs a fill — its presence drives the Managing state.

PriceBar.title: PriceBar
PriceBar.description:
One realized daily OHLCV bar in an episode's price window (the sparkline draws ``close``; the
full bar rides the wire so a later candlestick is a pure-frontend swap — no second contract change).
``close`` is non-null (null-close rows are skipped); ``open``/``high``/``low``/``volume`` are nullable
per-column — a close-only free-EOD bar surfaces them as ``null``, never invented (invariant #6).
``sma50``/``sma200`` are the trailing simple moving averages of ``close``, server-computed over a
warm-up read so the window's LEFT edge is honest; ``null`` where too little history precedes the bar
(a young security / early history) — an honest gap the context line simply begins after, never padded.

PriceIngestOut.title: PriceIngestOut
PriceIngestOut.description:
The per-security price pull's receipt (the finalize screen's decoupled price leg): how many EOD
bars appended (0 = already current — the ingest is incremental), how many overlap bars were
RE-VERSIONED (a source restatement, e.g. a split re-base — the exceptional path; source-strategy
Option A), and the latest bar now on file.

ProduceTermsRequest.title: ProduceTermsRequest
ProduceTermsRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /theses/{id}/terms`` (optional). ``seeds`` are the operator-anchored canonical compounds
(e.g. the known psychedelic compounds) — persisted as operator-authored SIGNAL, the recall guarantor against
keyword-gen non-determinism. Omitted / empty seeds -> regenerate preserves the thesis's EXISTING operator
seeds and just re-rolls the LLM-proposed terms.

PromoteIngestRef.title: PromoteIngestRef
PromoteIngestRef.description:
The promote response's ingest kick (PR-4): a promote that ADDED members starts their back-half
ingest (Form 4 + 8-K + 13D/G + EOD — the same per-thesis unit the cron runs, scoped to the new ids)
as a background job so a fresh basket needn't wait for the nightly cron. ``new_members`` is THIS
promote's newly-added count; the FE polls ``GET .../ingest/jobs/{job_id}``. Absent (``ingest`` null)
= nothing was added, nothing was kicked (the cost thread: every editor Save promotes, so only
genuinely-new names ever pay).

PromoteOnboardingRef.title: PromoteOnboardingRef
PromoteOnboardingRef.description:
X1 — the promote added COLD names (no other live basket holds them) that were QUEUED for the staged
onboarding job instead of ingested at once: more of them than the fast lane takes
(``Settings.onboard_fast_lane_max``), or the promote landed inside the nightly window. ``queued`` = this
promote's cold names now waiting (including any already queued), ``new_members`` = its newly-added count,
``reason`` = why they were queued. The FE polls ``GET .../onboarding`` for their progress.

PromoteOut.title: PromoteOut
PromoteOut.description:
The promote response: the saved ``ThesisDetail`` (the FE re-snapshot — unchanged) + the ADDITIVE
``ingest`` ref when this promote kicked a new-member ingest job (the fast lane), or the ADDITIVE
``onboarding`` ref when its cold names were queued for the staged onboarding job (X1). At most one of the
two is set. Optional/defaulted, so every pre-existing consumer of the promote response keeps its exact
shape.

PromoteThesisRequest.title: PromoteThesisRequest
PromoteThesisRequest.description:
The promote/update payload — a thesis-with-chain. The router builds a domain Thesis (the
segment-consistency validator runs) under the CURRENT tenant (the resolver, not the body), then upserts
it (create when `id` is null, update otherwise). Scores are NOT sent — they re-derive on read.
`authored_by` is honored from the body for the two live member values (`system_drafted` = the
description is a model draft / `operator_edited` = the operator changed it); the RETIRED
`operator_set` is legacy-translated to `signed_off=true` + `system_drafted`, never stored
(Discovery cleanup S1). `signed_off` (the per-name endorsement) round-trips as a marker — it never
gates promotion.

RadarSpacOut.title: RadarSpacOut
RadarSpacOut.description:
The SPAC Radar tape (``GET /radar/spac``): the latest version of each transition filing in
the window, newest first, with per-CIK deal state and per-thesis term matches. Pull-only and
quiet by design (#7 — a blank check is maximally early); every row links its filing (#6).

RatifyCatalyst.title: RatifyCatalyst
RatifyCatalyst.description:
A hand-authored catalyst-CONVICTION fact (the Key-1 arming path — ``fact_catalyst`` via
``ingest_catalyst``, ``source='ratified'``). Unlike the extractor-fed types there is no candidate:
the operator authors the event and MUST cite it (``source_ref`` — the press release / 8-K / IR
page; provenance is the point, #6). ``event_date`` = when the catalyst became known (valid time,
no lookahead); ``horizon_end`` optionally pins its relevance horizon (else the liveness default).
Distinct from the thesis-level catalyst SURFACE (display objects, ``PUT /theses/{id}/catalysts``).

ResolveEtfRequest.title: ResolveEtfRequest
ResolveEtfRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /workbench/securities/resolve-etf`` (ETF Sleeve, Slice 1) — the operator-supplied ETF
ticker to surface as a ``fund`` sleeve. Just the ticker: the server resolves it (lookup-or-create) and
marks it ``instrument_kind='etf'`` — operator-DECLARED, never auto-detected (#3, no LLM).

ResolvedPlacement.title: ResolvedPlacement
ResolvedPlacement.description:
A proposed name after resolution against the master. ``security_id`` is set IFF ``PLACED``;
``candidates`` is non-empty IFF ``AMBIGUOUS``. The model's ``prose`` is always preserved (display). Both
``name`` and ``ticker`` are BIND-THEN-LABEL: on a row that carries a ``security_id`` they are the BOUND
master row's SEC name + ticker (shown ≡ bound; ``_carry_identity_and_gate`` sets the name, promote persists
the ticker with the id) — never the model's echo; only an UNRESOLVED row (AMBIGUOUS / ABSENT) keeps the
model's proposed name + ticker guess (there is no bound row to label it from).

``matched_terms`` are the discovery keyword(s) the name's CIK hit (provenance — INVARIANT #6, and the
on-screen tell for a colliding seed per #9: a placed name shows WHY it surfaced). Empty for an off-universe
name resolved by the master rather than discovered by a term. Never a number (#3 — a keyword string).

``discovery_source`` records WHERE the name came from (provenance — INVARIANT #6): ``"edgar"`` = matched a
CIK in the EDGAR-discovered universe; ``"off_universe"`` = resolved OUTSIDE that universe, via the
sweep-augmented context. **It is NOT a hard claim the tail-sweep's web-search sourced the name** (``decompose``
may surface an off-universe name from its own knowledge) — it means only "off the deterministic universe,"
never "tail-sweep found this." Display-only like ``matched_terms``: never a number (#3), never promoted onto a
``BasketMember`` (#2). Defaults ``"edgar"`` (the conservative no-pill state) and is set ``"off_universe"`` in
exactly ONE place — the ``_match_discovered_cik`` fork — so a stray construction can never over-claim.

``sector`` / ``exchange`` / ``listing_status`` / ``category`` are machine-parsed IDENTITY carried from the master (enriched
just-in-time from EDGAR submissions before resolution) — display-only like ``matched_terms``: never a number
(#3), never promoted onto a ``BasketMember`` (#2). ``listing_status`` is a LISTING-PRESENCE heuristic
(``"active"`` / ``"inactive"``), NOT a delisting verdict: a PLACED name whose master row reads ``"inactive"``
is DOWNGRADED to AMBIGUOUS (never auto-placed) with its own row as the single pick — a frictionless rescue,
surfaced with a HEDGED flag ("no current listing found in EDGAR"), so a false-inactive costs one extra click,
never a silent drop (#9). ``None`` when the row is un-enriched (the honest fallback — no flag, no gate).

``off_thesis`` surfaces the NARRATOR's already-made "this name doesn't fit the thesis" opinion as a bit (the
``prose`` is the why) — display-only like ``matched_terms`` / ``discovery_source``: never a number (#3), never
promoted onto a ``BasketMember`` (#2), never on the call path. It RECOMMENDS, never removes: a flagged name
STAYS placed (membership is deterministic exact-CIK, #2 / #9 — never a silent drop) with a ``remove`` the
OPERATOR clicks (#10). Set at the narration MERGE (``app.routers.workbench.execute_draft``), not at resolution
— so it defaults ``False`` on every construction path here. COVERAGE = every placed/verify name: since the
prose reroute the organizer emits structure + assignment only, so organizer-placed and reconciler-appended
names alike arrive prose-less, are narrated (narration is the sole prose author), and can be flagged.
Fail-open: no narration → ``False`` (never flag on missing data).

RotationGroupOut.title: RotationGroupOut
RotationGroupOut.description:
One row of the map. Link view: ``link`` (``null`` = Unsegmented) + its card. Card view: the card.
Business type / Sector view: ``business_type`` / ``supersector`` (``null`` = Unclassified). ``names`` =
the companies in the group, each counted once.

RotationMapOut.title: RotationMapOut
RotationMapOut.description:
The whole page in one view, groups in the default order (the 7d median, highest first, "—" last).
The counts are the work shown on its quiet line. ``spy`` = SPY's own trailing returns (``null`` = no
SPY tape at the as-of). ``cache`` / ``compute_ms`` = whether the heavy read was served from the shared
dashboard cache and how long it took when it ran.

RotationNameCardOut.title: RotationNameCardOut
RotationNameCardOut.description:
A card a name sits on in this group: its ticker there (the Cockpit's ``?name=`` key) and its links
there (``null`` = Unsegmented).

RotationNameOut.title: RotationNameOut
RotationNameOut.description:
One company in a group. ``cross`` is its golden / death cross when it printed within ``cross_days``
of the as-of.

RotationWindowOut.title: RotationWindowOut
RotationWindowOut.description:
One return window of a group: the median over the names priced for it (``null`` when fewer than
``min_priced`` are), ``n`` priced, ``up`` of them with a positive return, ``above_spy`` of them beating
SPY's own return (``null`` without one). ``tone`` marks a median in the top / bottom 10% of the groups in
this view.

SavedRunSummary.title: SavedRunSummary
SavedRunSummary.description:
One saved draft-run artifact's summary for the run-loader picker (the cheap label fields — never the
draft itself; the detail endpoint returns the inner ``ChainDraftOut``). RUN metadata only: no score, no
number (#3). ``run_id`` is the artifact's filename stem (the detail-endpoint path segment).

ScoreboardEditionDiffResponse.title: ScoreboardEditionDiffResponse
ScoreboardEditionDiffResponse.description:
What changed from the EARLIER edition (``before``) to the LATER one (``after``), computed on read:
grouped thesis -> company, compared through ``through`` (the earlier of the two editions' last nights)
from ``first_night``, with the headline ``counts``. Substance only — state, the armed set, verdict,
grades, exit-by and each episode's score — never card text. ``causes`` (S7) = the later edition was cut
from the earlier one by the automatic cut, so every change carries a ``cause``.

ScoreboardEditionOut.title: ScoreboardEditionOut
ScoreboardEditionOut.description:
Which EDITION a Scoreboard read shows (editions S4). Edition 0 = the original record: the calls log,
never stored as an edition (``cut`` null — the record is append-only and current; ``first_night`` /
``last_night`` = the calls log's first / latest as-of; no join dates, so the entry counts are null and the
engine fields too). Edition N >= 1 = a stored re-run of today's rules from each company's join date on
the public clock, frozen at ``cut`` (the newest row it could hold): ``causes`` names why it was cut
(``initial`` for Edition 1), ``n_entries_estimated`` of ``n_entries`` join dates are option-A estimates,
and the engine fingerprint / policy hash / code sha say which rules and code produced it (``code_sha``
null when unknown, never fabricated).

ScoreboardEditionsResponse.title: ScoreboardEditionsResponse
ScoreboardEditionsResponse.description:
Every edition the Scoreboard can show, Edition 0 (the original record) first, then each stored
edition ascending; ``default`` = the edition a ``GET /scoreboard`` with no ``edition`` serves.
``notice`` (S7) = the quiet line for seven days after the automatic cut published the newest edition
(null otherwise).

ScoreboardEpisodeOut.title: ScoreboardEpisodeOut
ScoreboardEpisodeOut.description:
One arm episode from the record, scored — a ledger row. Outcome fields keep replay's
canonical names (``forward_return`` = arm→exit_by on realized closes ≤ the request asof).
``status``/``matured``/``censored_start`` are the record-honesty flags: open = a RUNNING
return, not a verdict; metrics judge only matured + non-censored episodes.

The excursion pair reports how far the episode ran each way before its exit, on two bases:
``peak_*``/``trough_*`` are CLOSE-based (maximum favorable / adverse excursion, MFE / MAE — the
same basis as ``forward_return``), and ``intraday_high_*``/``intraday_low_*`` are the WICK
extremes, null unless every bar in the window carries the column (they never fall back to the
close). ``path`` is the window's closes, ascending — variable length, one episode's own span, so
two rows' paths share no time axis; ``dearm_index`` marks the de-arm on it, null when the de-arm
fell outside the scored window. All descriptive: no metric reads them.

``truncated`` = the episode's horizon extends past the end of THIS NAME'S price tape
(``exit_by > tape_edge(name)``, read within the request as-of). It asks the tape, never the
calendar: an ``exit_by`` that fell on a weekend or a market holiday sits before a live name's
tape edge, so nothing was missed and the flag is false. A still-running episode is truncated by
construction (the as-of caps the tape edge too) and several render sites depend on that to
phrase a running return honestly.

``tape_behind_market`` is the LOUDNESS half — ``truncated`` and the market printed past this
horizon anyway (``exit_by < tape_edge(market)``, the latest bar anywhere in the tenant's tape
under the same caps). Strictly narrower: it drops the two cases where falling short is not this
name's fault — an episode maturing today (no close exists until after the bell) and a globally
stalled feed (nobody is starved; that is the record-freshness alarm). What is left is a name
genuinely behind the market, and it is what the ledger badge gates on, together with
``matured``. The field states the fact; this states whether the fact is worth shouting.

ScoreboardMetricOut.title: ScoreboardMetricOut
ScoreboardMetricOut.description:
One claim-tied metric (the replay set, computed over eligible live outcomes). ``claim``
names which system claim it tests — never a generic hit-rate; below ``n``/``insufficient_n``
the summary must not be read as a claim (the FE renders it quiet).

ScoreboardPriceWindowOut.title: ScoreboardPriceWindowOut
ScoreboardPriceWindowOut.description:
One episode's realized daily OHLCV series over ``[start, end]``, CAPPED at ``asof`` server-side —
the drawer sparkline's on-demand read (Slice 3, extended in Slice A, widened in Slice B). It is the
SAME asof-capped window the scorer runs (``PgRealizedPrices`` — ``bars_between`` shares
``closes_between``'s cap/known_at), exposed on request rather than embedded in the ledger payload.
Each bar also carries ``sma50``/``sma200`` context, and four dated event families ride beside the
bars, ALL under the identical two-axis no-lookahead discipline (valid_from window + the
``recorded_at`` knowability gate): ``insider_buys`` (code-P purchases, each carrying its
server-classified ``character``, set-aside rows riding grayed-and-labeled rather than hidden — Band
03 S2c), ``insider_sells`` (the code-S mirror, Slice B), ``corporate_events`` (every stored 8-K —
no server-side item cut), and ``activist_stakes`` (the 13D/G tape, unresolved identity shipped as
null, never dropped). Invariant #1: no bar with ``d > asof`` and no event recorded after the as-of
is ever returned, whatever ``end`` the client passes. ``source`` names the fact table the bars came
from (invariant #6). ``start`` is the EFFECTIVE relevance floor the server computed
(``max(thesis.created_at − 365d, first_bar)``), NOT the requested start — the loaded extent the
FE numbers the overlay universe over (Slice A R1).

ScoreboardReplayThesisOut.title: ScoreboardReplayThesisOut
ScoreboardReplayThesisOut.description:
One thesis's replayed, scored arm episodes — the `/backtest` run ledger's per-thesis slice (the name
survives from the Scoreboard's replay-alongside panel, retired by editions S8). Platform track only:
decision capture post-dates history, so the operator column is structurally absent, not empty.

ScoreboardResponse.title: ScoreboardResponse
ScoreboardResponse.description:
The Scoreboard: one EDITION scored as-of ``asof`` — Edition 0 is the call-of-record (the record, never
a recompute); Edition N >= 1 is a stored re-run, read from its frozen pages (``edition`` says which).

ScoreboardSummaryOut.title: ScoreboardSummaryOut
ScoreboardSummaryOut.description: The aggregate strip: counts + the honesty banner + the gated metric set.

ScoreboardThesisOut.title: ScoreboardThesisOut
ScoreboardThesisOut.description:
One thesis's slice of the Scoreboard: record coverage + scored episodes. Present even at
zero episodes — the record span and an accruing warming window ARE the honest launch state.
``record_error`` surfaces an unreadable historical card (fault isolation), never a 500.

ScoredFigureOut.title: ScoredFigureOut
ScoredFigureOut.description:
One meter/figure on the wire: the 0-4 pip (null = "—"/no data), the raw value, and the provenance
chips ("behind the scores"). market_cap carries `value` only (pips null — a figure, not a meter).

ScoredMemberOut.title: ScoredMemberOut
ScoredMemberOut.description: A basket member scored for the Workbench — the four meters + the market-cap figure + the fit label.

SecurityCandidate.title: SecurityCandidate
SecurityCandidate.description: A master row offered for the operator to pick (ticker + CIK shown so a homonym is disambiguated).

SecurityMatchOut.title: SecurityMatchOut
SecurityMatchOut.description:
A security-master match for the Workbench's add-a-name typeahead (Slice 4b) AND the surface-ETF
resolve receipt (ETF Sleeve, Slice 1). The operator picks the exact row; its ``security_id`` is then
placed into the basket. A discovery net over the EXISTING per-tenant master (INVARIANT #2) — every match
is a real member, nothing is ingested or guessed.

``instrument_kind`` is what the row IS — ``equity`` (the typeahead default) or ``etf`` (returned by the
surface-ETF resolve so the FE adds it as a ``fund`` sleeve). Identity, never a call input (#4/#6).

Segment.title: Segment
Segment.description:
A link in the thesis's value chain (the Workbench decomposition) — STRUCTURE, not a score.

The per-segment candidate count is DERIVED on read (``len`` of members in the link), never stored.

SetBusinessTypeRequest.title: SetBusinessTypeRequest
SetBusinessTypeRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /workbench/securities/{security_id}/business-type`` — the operator's per-security
business-type RE-TAG (Business-Type M1). ``business_type`` is the leaf to tag, or ``null`` to CLEAR the
re-tag (the visible revert back to the maps-derived classification — reversibility, WB #1). Identity
metadata, never a fact (#3); the server stores it ONLY when it differs from the derived leaf (0033
store-on-diff) and stamps ``operator:retag`` as the basis.

SharedNameChipOut.title: SharedNameChipOut

SharedNameRowOut.title: SharedNameRowOut
SharedNameRowOut.description:
